## D851. The project's performance-bonus pool (#330, 2026-10-12)

The install project's `performanceBonusPool` is set to the record's 5% payout (at cost). It is synced after the status
transaction commits, on a win, a re-win and every rebuild, and kept as it is if the quote later leaves Won.

## D852. Small deviations (#330, 2026-10-12)

- The two locked bonus rows sit at the end of each system's line table; they stand in for the spec's footer line.
- The internal cost summary shows the 5% payout (cost), not its marked-up sell.
- The Reports → Estimator bonuses report reads only records, so a quote won before this shipped is absent until Record now.
- The report's CSV export has no formula-injection guard. None of the app's CSVs have one; that is a codebase-wide gap,
  flagged in PUNCHLIST #330 rather than fixed in one export.

## D853. Estimates always print the full Peak letterhead (#331, 2026-10-12)

The estimate document (the PDF, the staff preview and the online page), the client package page and the Cover PDF always
head with the full baked Peak letterhead sheet (`peak-letterhead.jpg`), even when Settings → Branding has a dark logo
uploaded. Letters, reports and the other D59 / D823 outputs keep the uploaded-logo ladder. `logoDark` stays on
`QuoteDocumentProps` (it is Branding data other callers read) but the estimate never prints it. The Grid notes #9
Peak-header toggle (D824) still does not apply to the estimate document. Left open for Jeff: whether the
estimate package zip's `Specifications.docx` and `Datasheets.pdf` cover, and the client-style curtain cut sheets, should
switch to the full sheet too (they still follow the ladder). Punch item #331.

## D854. An assembly line expands to its members for datasheets and the package BOM (#332, 2026-10-12)

One shared, client-safe pure helper, `src/lib/quote-line-members.ts` (`expandLine`, `specItems`, `needsFixtureLookup`),
decides what an Estimator line stands for:
- a **rack** line (`rackId`) reads its **live** members (D578) or returns null — rack gone, not a rack, member-less, or no
  lookup — so the quoted rack row stays. It never falls back to `components`, which for a rack holds only the rack-level
  parts;
- any other line with a stored `components` snapshot expands to those parts × the line's qty; optional add-ons (qty 0)
  and labor are left out;
- else an `asm:` / portal `fixtureId` / bare fixture line resolves live through `gridSpecBomRows`.

`quoteBom` (client package and package documents), `specPackageDocs`, `bomFromQuote` (now like its Grid branch), Customer
review's Datasheets tab, Catalog → Datasheets and the photo sheet (Estimator components; Grid `asm:` lines and placements
through the fixtures) list the members instead of the `SA-` row. Racks and tracks expand for datasheets like any other
assembly. Punch item #332.

## D855. Photos and narrative paragraphs alias a fixture assembly to its primary member (#332, 2026-10-12)

`isAssemblyLine` is the one predicate for the photo / paragraph / key-product datasheet alias: `fixture: true` or a portal
`fixtureId` — fixture, System and Hardware assemblies — never a rack (`rackId`) and never a track (a `track` config or a
`TRK-` sku). `primaryMemberSku` is the light engine, else the first included part, read only from the line's own
`components` snapshot (no fixture lookup), so the browser (`kpAliases` in the Estimator state) and the server
(`narrative/photos.ts`, `specPackageDocs`' `aliases`) run the same pure function on the same line. A starred assembly
prints its member's photo (else the manufacturer image, D583), stored under the line's sku; the package page and staff
preview copy the member's datasheet onto the line (`withDatasheetAliases`, beside #304's moved aliases). The narrative
column shows the member's paragraph and photo (`viaSku`), and **Save to library / Save to product write to that member
part**, not to the assembly. The key-product library caches by (sku, alias) (`libraryFetchKey` / `libraryStaleSkus`), so a
changed alias under the same sku refetches. Punch item #332.

## D856. No zip cache bump for #332 (#332, 2026-10-12)

`PACKAGE_ZIP_CACHE_VERSION` is unchanged (still 3). An estimate package zip already cached in Blob for a sent revision
keeps the contents it was built with (the `SA-` row, no member datasheets) until its cache file goes; a zip not yet
cached, or a revision sent after this ships, gets the members. The online package page and the doc route read live and
show the members at once. Whether to bump the version (which rebuilds every cached zip on its next download) is left to
Jeff, flagged in PUNCHLIST #332.

## D857. Build package has three tabs (#333, 2026-10-12)

Narrative · BOM quote · Client package, at `?ptab=narrative|bom|client`. Narrative is the default and writes no param; an
unknown or wrong-case value reads as Narrative, and `ptab` is ignored off the package step. `stepSearch` drops `ptab`
whenever it writes another step. Tabs switch with `pushState` (arrow keys `replaceState`), roving tabindex like the review
tabs. The Narrative tab stays mounted while hidden (`display:none`), so the TipTap editor keeps its undo history and the
Phase 5 unmount flush isn't exercised by a tab switch; BOM quote and Client package mount on first visit. The staff panel
splits into a documents part (Client package) and a grid part (Design in the Grid stays on Narrative). Punch item #333.

Jeff confirmed Q4. A system's Narrative | Itemized choice is set only in Client package → Systems (every system with
items; an unpriced one is marked "No price yet — not on the PDF"). The narrative column shows it read-only with a link,
and the Build system card's select becomes a read-only "Customer: Narrative ↗" chip linking to
`?step=package&ptab=client#systems`. Draft narrative's automatic switch to Narrative stays (it writes the same field).

## D859. The BOM quote tab is built in the browser (#333, 2026-10-12)

`liveBomDocumentProps` = `bomViewProps(quoteDocumentDataFor(…))` over the unsaved editor state, the same pure builder the
print route and preview use; no server action, no debounce. `rewardsLine` comes from the credit read
(`purchasePerksDocLine`) when it is for the same customer. The tab is code-split (`next/dynamic`), renders with the scoped
`QUOTE_WEB_EMBED_CSS`, freezes behind a memoised document while hidden, and labels itself "Live" with Open saved preview ↗
for a saved estimate. A harness check pins equivalence with the saved render and the #330 no-bonus rule. Punch item
#333.

## D860. `Quote.packageSelection` has one writer and is frozen per revision (#333, 2026-10-12)

`packageSelection` (`estimatePdf`, `coverPdf`, `drawings`, `excludedDatasheets`) is not a content field: a change never
stales the PDF or an approval. As shipped it differs from the spec (which had it also riding Save):
- after create its **only** writer is `setPackageSelection` (store), reached through `updateQuoteMetaAction`. Save never
  carries it and `update()` drops it, so a Save built before a newer tick can't revert it;
- the patch is checked (`checkSelectionPatch`): null / non-object is ignored; only the fields present are merged over the
  stored value under the row lock; a SKU over 200 characters or more than 500 exclusions is **refused** with a reason,
  never truncated. Read-side `normalizePackageSelection` still defaults junk;
- a write never bumps `updatedAt` (the `setPackagePeakHeader` precedent), so it can't fail an in-flight Send's version
  check;
- left-out SKUs follow #304 renames at write (`selectionFollowingRenames`) and at read (`moved`);
- a new estimate holds the choice in state; its first Save flushes it only when it was edited, so an untouched estimate
  never gains the key; a later Save retries a failed write.

It is frozen into a new revision's `docFields.packageSelection` only when the live quote has one, so untouched quotes'
revisions are byte-identical, and it is never annexed after send (unlike `packageFiles`). Absent means today's behaviour.
Punch item #333.

## D861. Estimate / Cover PDF switches are Send & track defaults; Send waits for the choices (#333, 2026-10-12)

Jeff confirmed Q5: the switches only set whether Send & track's "Estimate PDF" and "Cover PDF" start ticked
(`composerInitial(d, sel)`); the sender can still change them per send, and nothing is added to the client's package page.
Send awaits `selectionSettled()`, which races a 10 s timeout and reports whether the server holds the latest choice; if
not, Send is blocked with "Couldn't save the package choices … nothing was sent", so a revision never freezes a choice the
server doesn't hold. Punch item #333.

Client package → Documents' "BOM (itemized) appendix" and "Cut sheets" rows are `pdfOptions.pdfItemizedAppendix` /

folders are unchanged. Punch item #333.

For a revision sent with drawings off, the package page shows no Plans & risers and the file route returns its uniform 404
(`revisionShownPackageFiles`); the staff preview follows the live choice, the "No drawings" gap chip is suppressed, and

Jeff confirmed Q1: datasheets only — spec sheets and manuals still ship. An exclusion is keyed by live SKU. One pure rule,

opts)`: "self" when the SKU is left out, "parent" when its datasheet is covered and **every** covering parent is left out
(an accessory follows its fixture). Excluded counts as satisfied (no gap, so unticking a Missing row means "not needed on
this project"); its document reaches `documents` only through an included SKU. The list is never auto-pruned. With no
`opts` the output is deep-equal to before (pinned on committed fixtures). Every datasheet consumer honours it: package docs,
the doc route, the gap chip, the book, the zip, the Quotes-hub package and Customer review's rows ("Left out of this
package" / "Left out with S4-26"). Punch item #333.

## D868. Live datasheet rows from a trimmed BOM projection (#333, 2026-10-12)

The Client package tab's Datasheets column is built from the **unsaved** BOM: a `BomProjection` of only the keys `quoteBom`
and the member expansion read, sent to `clientPackageDocsAction` with no exclusions applied (the browser applies
`datasheetExclusion`, so a tick is instant). It runs only while the tab is shown, debounced 800 ms after the projection key
changes, sequence-guarded (latest wins). The server re-sanitises (≤ 200 sections, ≤ 5,000 items, strings ≤ 300). As
shipped, the projection is also byte-budgeted (900 kB) under the server-action ceiling; anything cut shows "List truncated
— N items not checked" (client and server counts). Assembly members indent under "Part of: …" (D854); `partOf` comes from
the member expansion, not the removed `lineMemberRows`. Punch item #333.

## D869. The Assist gate — opt-in, an empty list means nobody (#334, 2026-10-12)

A button renders, and its server action runs, only when all of these hold: `ASSIST_DISABLED` is not `"true"`; a provider
is configured (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `ASSIST_PROVIDER=local` with `ASSIST_LOCAL_URL`); `settings.assistUsers` includes
the user's id; `settings.assistFeatures[feature]` is not `false` (a missing key is on); and the thread is an email thread
the user can see. **An empty `assistUsers` list means nobody**, the opposite of `recordingsBetaUsers`, so merging this
switches nothing on. `assistGate` is a pure function over (feature, user id, settings, env); `assistUiFlags` feeds the
Inbox reader; the action re-checks on the server and returns `{ ok:false, error }` with no network call when the gate
fails. With no key the layer is inert and nothing renders. Thread access is one shared read, `loadThreadFor`
(`src/lib/assist/thread-access.ts`): a live email thread in the user's own mailbox. Punch item #334.
Verified: gate truth table in `scripts/test-assist.ts` (empty list, kill switch, missing provider, feature off, each
passing); smoke renders Inbox / Estimator / Settings sections with no key and no Assist UI.

## D870. Per-feature model routing and a cost table (#334, 2026-10-12)

Tasks and the estimate's extract step run on `claude-haiku-5-5` (low effort), Draft reply on `claude-sonnet-5-5` (low),
the estimate draft on `claude-opus-5-5` (medium, 32,000 max tokens, **streamed**). Env overrides: `ASSIST_MODEL_TASKS`,
`ASSIST_MODEL_REPLY`, `ASSIST_MODEL_EXTRACT`, `ASSIST_MODEL_ESTIMATE`. **Each slot carries its own request budget**
(`SLOT_SETTINGS.timeoutMs` / `maxRetries`, passed per request through `requestOptionsFor` — the SDK retries timeouts too, so
a slot's worst case is timeout × (retries + 1)): tasks and reply 60 s / 1 retry, extract 45 s / 0, the estimate draft
210 s / 0. Extract + draft (255 s worst case) fit the Inbox page's `maxDuration = 300`, and `draftEstimateFromThread`
refuses before the draft call when less than `DRAFT_MIN_REMAINING_MS` (220 s) of `ESTIMATE_BUDGET_MS` (300 s) is left
(logged, and stamped `draftSkipped` on the extract run). The non-draft slots go through `client.beta.messages.create(params,
{ timeout, maxRetries })`; the draft goes through `client.beta.messages.stream(params, opts).finalMessage()` (0.128.0
accepts `betas` and `fallbacks` on both) so adaptive thinking can't push it into "too long", with its own wall-clock abort
because the SDK timeout stops at the response headers. `fallbacks:"default"` plus the `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` beta ride only on
`claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5` and `claude-fable-5-1` (Haiku has none). The `thinking` param is
never sent (the models are adaptive by default, and `disabled` 400s on Sonnet and Opus) and `tool_choice` is never forced;
effort goes in `output_config.effort` and JSON in `output_config.format = {type:"json_schema"}` built from `z.strictObject`
schemas. The system prompt is one `cache_control: ephemeral` block. Cost is `claudeCostUsd(response.model, requested,
usage)` from a `MODEL_PRICES` table (Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, Opus 5 at $5/$25, Fable 5.1 at $10/$50; Haiku steps
up past 100K input tokens; cache-write 1.25× and Haiku cache-read 0.1× are assumed rates), so every report cost is
labelled estimated. **A Claude run never costs $0 by accident**: an answering model missing from the table (a server-side
fallback or a dated alias) bills at the requested model's row, and when that is unknown too, at the dearest row in the
table. A local run costs $0.
This is the beta path only — no deterministic feature changed. Punch item #334.
Verified: cost math (including the Haiku >100K step and the answered → requested → dearest rule, end to end through
`runAssist`), `buildAnthropicParams` (the exact params object, with no `thinking` and no `tool_choice`), `requestOptionsFor`
/ `anthropicRequestOptions` per slot, the 300 s fit and the 220 s refusal asserted in `scripts/test-assist.ts`; no network.

## D871. One provider interface; Claude by default, a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint later (#334, 2026-10-12)

`AssistProvider.complete(req)` has two implementations: `anthropic.ts` (the official `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, one lazy client
per key with no client-wide timeout — timeout and retries are per request from the slot (D870), so `ASSIST_TIMEOUT_MS` is
gone; typed errors mapped to short messages, a timeout reads "timed out"; `refusal` and `max_tokens` stop reasons read
before content) and `local.ts` (`POST {ASSIST_LOCAL_URL}/v1/chat/completions`, Bearer
token, its own timeout; Ollama / LM Studio / MLX on the Mac mini; cost $0). With `ASSIST_PROVIDER=local` the Anthropic
provider is the fallback when a key exists: an unreachable local endpoint re-runs once on **Haiku 5.5** for every feature
(Jeff's call) and the row logs `fellBack:true`. Tests inject a `FakeProvider` through `runAssist`'s deps. The live SDK call
is not run in dev (no key); the first real call is the Jeff-gated pilot step. Punch item #334.
Verified: provider selection and the fallback path in `scripts/test-assist.ts` with `FakeProvider`; `anthropic.ts` checked

## D872. `runAssist` order and the `assist_runs` table (#334, 2026-10-12)

Every model call runs through `runAssist`: gate, then the monthly cap (`monthSpend(Chicago month) >= assistMonthlyCapUsd`,
default $200; no row is written), then the rate limit (`assist:<feature>:<user>`, per hour: tasks 60, reply 60, estimate
20; **the estimate counts once per button press, on the extract step — the draft step passes `countRate:false`**), then the
provider (with the local → Haiku fallback), then `JSON.parse` + zod `safeParse` ("unreadable answer" on failure), and last
a log row, written whether the call succeeded or failed. `assist_runs` is a doc table (migration `0039_assist_runs`,
idempotent) holding feature, step, user, provider, requested and served model, `fellBack`, the four token counts, cost,
latency, an input hash, the raw output (capped at 20,000 chars), ok/error/stop reason, `contextRef`, the Chicago
`monthKey`, and an outcome (`accepted | edited | discarded`) with detail. `setRunOutcome` is first-write-wins and own-user
only, atomically. The table is in `DOC_TABLES` and `CONFIG_COLLECTIONS`, so the go-live wipe keeps the trial's history and
its spend. `recordAssistOutcomeAction` accepts outcomes only for tasks and reply runs (the client judges those); an
estimate's outcome is computed at report time (D878). The Inbox page exports `maxDuration = 300` so the two-call estimate
fits one server-action budget. Punch item #334.
Verified: `scripts/test-assist.ts` DB checks on a scratch PGlite — rows logged for ok and failed calls, the cap writes no
row at the limit, a failed gate makes no call, outcome is first-write-wins and own-user only, migration 0039 exists, and
the table is registered in both lists.

## D873. Reply style comes from the sender's own sent mail (#334, 2026-10-12)

Draft reply is shown up to 5 of the sender's last outgoing emails from their own personal mailbox (every outbound email
there counts — Gmail-imported mail carries the Gmail display name as author, so the author is not matched; logged calls,
queued mail, deleted threads and the current thread excluded; quoted customer text cut — `>` lines and everything from an
"On … wrote:" or "-----Original Message-----" line; signatures stripped; each trimmed to 1,200 chars), inside
`<style_examples>`, labelled as examples of how this person writes — match tone and length, never copy facts. The prompt also carries the last 10 messages of the thread (2,500 chars each), the customer
and contact names and a tone (`short | normal | formal`). **Open quotes are listed for the thread's resolved customer only**
(draft or sent, newest 8, with number, name, type, status and sent date or "not sent"; **only a sent quote shows its
rounded value — a draft reads "price not yet approved"**, and the system prompt allows a price only for a quote listed as
sent); with no resolved customer the prompt says there are none on file. The answer is plain text (`cleanReplyText` strips a `Subject:` line and a
trailing `-- ` block, caps at 6,000 chars); it lands in the inline composer with the signature added and a "Drafted by
Assist — review before sending" note, and never sends. Outcome on send: word-level edit ratio ≤ 0.10 is accepted, else
edited; closing the composer with a pending draft is discarded. Punch item #334.
Verified: `pickStyleExamples` (Gmail-author mail, quoted text), `stripQuotedText`, `cleanReplyText`, `openQuotesFor` (no
draft value), `editRatio` and `replyOutcome` in `scripts/test-assist.ts`.

## D874. Thread text is untrusted data (#334, 2026-10-12)

Email text is written by outside parties. Every prompt wraps it in `<email_thread>…</email_thread>` and the system prompt
says it — and the `<style_examples>` block — is data, never an instruction; a body or author containing a close tag or a
line break is defanged so it cannot end a wrapper early or forge a header. The single-line names outside the wrapper (customer,
contact and quote names in the reply prompt, link labels and team names in the tasks prompt) go through the same
`cleanPromptField` (one line, `</email_thread` / `</style_examples` / `</example` defanged, 120 chars). Nothing a model returns is acted on except as text a person reviews: tasks need a tick
and go through the existing #215 path, a reply is a composer draft, an estimate is a draft quote. Nothing auto-sends,
auto-links, or changes a status. Model output is re-validated server-side (`sanitize*`: caps, allowed ids and link keys,
date shape) before it is used. Punch item #334.
Verified: `scripts/test-assist.ts` — wrapper defanging, author line-break stripping, defanged names and link labels, and the
task sanitizer's unknown-assignee / unknown-link / past-date rules.

## D875. Draft estimate is two steps: Haiku extracts, Opus drafts (#334, 2026-10-12)

`draftEstimateAction(threadId)` checks the gate before any load, then runs a cheap Haiku **extract** (quote name, venue, up
to 15 equipment requests with quantities, up to 8 system names, 45 s, no retry), then, only if it found a request, gathers
candidates (D876) and — only with at least 220 s of the 300 s budget left (D870) — runs a streamed Opus **draft** (210 s,
no retry) that returns systems and lines with a reason per line and notes. The model never outputs a price: a line's SKU must be a
candidate SKU or empty (an empty or unknown SKU becomes a custom line flagged "Assist: needs a part and price"), quantities
are integers 1–9999, at most 12 systems and 60 lines each. `buildDraftSections` (pure) turns the answer into `SpecItem`
sections: catalog lines are priced only by `catalogAddPrice(cost, list, tierMargin)`, systems take `priceRound` of $25 like
the Estimator's own new-system path, and **line ids are unique across the whole drafted quote** (the Estimator finds and
removes a line by id alone). It reports `dropped` (blank lines removed) and `unresolved` (SKUs outside the candidate set,
kept only as custom lines). Punch item #334.
Verified: `buildDraftSections` checks in `scripts/test-assist.ts` — candidate-only SKUs, custom lines for unknowns, prices
from `catalogAddPrice` and never from model output, unique line ids across systems, `priceRound`.

## D876. Candidates come from four sources and carry no money (#334, 2026-10-12)

The draft sees only parts the server found: (1) the Estimator's own catalog ranking for each requested phrase (the logic of
`searchCatalog` extracted as `rankCatalogParts` so it runs without a request scope; `searchCatalog` calls the shared
function), top 8 each; (2) similar past systems from the system library; (3) this customer's last five system quotes
(Daylite history excluded); (4) the system categories with their typical items. Every SKU is resolved through
`getManyBySku`, which follows model-number renames (D636–D642); a SKU with no live part is dropped, and the list given to
the model is `{ sku, desc, mfr, unit, category }`, capped at 400 parts, with no cost or price. **Category items and example
lines take their seats in the cap first; catalog hits fill the rest** (`selectCandidateParts`), so a long search can't
crowd out a category's typical items. Example lines and category items are shown under their **live (renamed) SKU**, and a
line whose SKU didn't resolve or didn't make the cap is dropped (`remapExampleLines`) — the model never sees a SKU it may
not use. Punch item #334.
Verified: `rankCatalogParts`, `selectCandidateParts`, `remapExampleLines` and the draft prompt in `scripts/test-assist.ts` —
candidates found by description, priority seats and renamed SKUs, and the draft prompt text carries no cost or price figure
(the DB-level check greps the prompt for the part's cost and list).

## D877. A draft is an ordinary Estimator quote with an `assistDraft` marker (#334, 2026-10-12)

The result is created through the same chain as a new estimate (`resolveTier`, `canonicalBonusSections`, `totals`,
`create`, then `scheduleQuotePdf`) with `source: "estimator"`, `status: "draft"`, `owner` and `preparedBy` the requesting
user. **It gets no `leadId`**, even when the thread is linked to a lead: a lead link would carry the lead's estimate number
(#223) onto a throw-away draft and stretch "no auto-link"; the thread reference lives in `assistDraft.threadId` only. Because the source stays `"estimator"`, bonuses (D846–D852), approval
(D517–D520), the library and every report behave as for a hand-built estimate. The only trace is the optional
`Quote.assistDraft { runId, threadId, at, notes, reasons, dismissedAt? }`. The thread's own link is **not** changed. Once
`create` has returned, a later failure (the `assistDraft` write) is logged, the run still records `quoteId` (in a
`finally`), and the action returns the quote — the user is never invited to retry into a duplicate. The action returns
the builder href and the client navigates there; the button is guarded against a double click. Punch item #334.

`source:"estimator"`, `assistDraft` set, thread link unchanged, and no `leadId` on a lead-linked thread's draft.

## D878. The draft banner, Dismiss, and an outcome computed at report time (#334, 2026-10-12)

The Estimator shows "Drafted from an email by Assist — check every line before submitting" with a link back to the thread,
the model's notes and a collapsible "Why these parts" list for lines that still exist. **Dismiss** sets
`assistDraft.dismissedAt` through `dismissAssistDraft`, which does not bump the quote's `updatedAt` (a dismiss is not an
edit, so it cannot make an in-flight save or an approval go stale). An estimate stores no outcome: the report compares the
run's drafted `[{sku, qty}]` with the quote's materials lines now (`estimateKeep`: kept, changed, removed) — accepted at
≥ 90 % kept, discarded when the quote is gone or under 10 % kept-or-changed, else edited. A run whose detail has an
explicit `quoteId: null` (no systems built, or the create failed) is discarded; a run with no `quoteId` key yet is pending
(`estimateOutcomeFor`). `loadAssistVM` reads the quotes in parallel and never throws — on a DB error (a preview deploy can
reach the shared database before migration 0039) the card shows an empty report instead of a 500. Punch item #334.
Verified: `estimateKeep` thresholds, `estimateOutcomeFor` (null = discarded, absent = pending) and `dismissAssistDraft`
(no `updatedAt` change, idempotent) in `scripts/test-assist.ts`.

`app_settings` gains `assistUsers` (default `[]`), `assistFeatures` (default `{}`; a missing key is on) and

## D880. The SDK supersedes D39 for this layer; D89's deletions stay deleted; the Assist gate replaces "no model calls" (#334, 2026-10-12)

Three things, stated together because they touch the same earlier decisions. (1) **D39** ("no new npm dependency — Anthropic
over plain fetch") is superseded for this layer only: Assist uses the official `@anthropic-ai/sdk` (0.128.0, beta messages)
for typed errors, retries and the fallback beta. (2) **D89**'s deletions stay deleted — the thread and customer summaries,

(3) **D89's "no model calls remain" posture is replaced by the opt-in Assist gate**: with no key, an empty pilot list, or
`ASSIST_DISABLED=true`, the app makes zero model calls and renders no Assist UI, exactly as under D89; with the gate open

## D881. The Claude key can be pasted in Settings; the saved key wins over the env var, except on previews (#334 follow-up, 2026-10-13)

An admin (`manage_users`) pastes the Claude API key in Settings → Beta → Assist pilot → **Claude API key** instead of
setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in Vercel. **Precedence** (pure `effectiveAnthropicKey`, `src/lib/assist/config.ts`): a
readable saved key wins; else the env var (trimmed); else none. **On a Vercel preview** (`VERCEL_ENV=preview`) the saved
key is ignored unless `ASSIST_ALLOW_PREVIEW_KEY=true` — previews share the production DB and must not spend on it; an env
var set on the preview still applies. **Storage**: `src/lib/assist/key-store.ts` encrypts with `encryptWith` (AES-256-GCM,
keyed on `AUTH_SECRET`) into its own `blobs` row `assist_secrets` (`anthropicKeyEnc`, `last4`, `savedAt`, `savedBy`) — not
`app_settings`, so the ciphertext never rides along in settings props; Remove nulls the fields (`setBlob` merges). A
decrypt failure (e.g. `AUTH_SECRET` rotated) falls back to the env var and the card says "Saved key can't be read —
re-enter it". The decrypted read is cached in-process for 30 s and dropped on save/remove. **Wiring**: `getAssistEnv()`
returns the base env with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` replaced by the effective key; `runAssist` uses it only when the caller
passed no `env` (tests that pass `env` never see the saved key), and the Inbox page's UI flags, the Inbox actions'
early gate and the Settings status line read it too. **Never to the browser**: no action returns the key, the card gets
`AssistKeyInfo` (source, last four, saved at/by, unreadable, preview-ignored), the input is a never-prefilled password
field, and errors never echo it. **Test key** makes one free `models.retrieve("claude-haiku-5-5")` call (15 s, no
retries, 20 per hour per admin) and writes no `assist_runs` row. A leaked key must be revoked in the Anthropic Console —
Remove only stops this app using it (other server instances may keep it for up to ~30 s). No migration, no new required
env var. Punch item #334.
Verified (2026-10-13): `test:assist` 197 PASS / 0 FAIL (37 new `assistKeyChecks`: `cleanApiKey`, the precedence truth
table incl. preview / preview + allow / unreadable, ciphertext-only blob, wrong secret = unreadable, `getAssistEnv`,
`assistKeyInfo` never carrying a key, clear nulls every field, an explicit empty `env` to `runAssist` stays closed with a
key saved); tsc 0 errors; eslint 0 problems on the 11 changed source/test files; `next build` OK (137 static pages);
`test:specs` 18,065 PASS / 0 FAIL ("ALL PASSED"); `test:smoke` 245 / 245, incl. /settings?section=data and /inbox 200.

## D882. The filing pipeline: sender rule → identity → numbers → noise → Haiku; a weak domain guess ranks after numbers (#335, 2026-10-13)

Every thread that gains a message is organized (`organizeThread`, `src/lib/inbox-org/pipeline.ts`) in a fixed order, first
match wins: a saved **sender rule** (exact address, then domain; personal beats company), the existing **identity** match
(a contact-email match is strong), a **record number** (`EST|FLM|RIG|REP|RNT|CON|OPP-####` incl. `-2`/`-3`, then project and
lead ids; subject first, then body; a number that doesn't resolve to a live record is ignored), the **noise rules**, and
for pilot owners **Haiku**. Spec §1 says "first match wins"; I read a **weak domain guess as a fallback ranked below numbers
and noise**, because the AI step treats "only weak" as unresolved. A strong identity takes a number only when the number
points at the same customer's record (the filing becomes identity plus work). An unresolved thread is stored as
`{customerId: null, work: null, noise: false, strength: "weak", state: "suggested"}` and shows in To file. Forwards: the
forwarded sender drives filing only when the forwarder is internal; a customer forwarding a third party's mail stays filed
under the customer; the original subject is always scanned for numbers. The suggestion lives on `CommThread.filing`; a
`filed`/`dismissed` filing is kept (only `needsReply` refreshes), `skipped` and an AI suggestion are kept until new
outside mail. Rule suggestions append to the capped `inbox_filing_log` blob only when they change. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` pipeline checks — number in subject/body, dead number, rule beats identity,
number-beats-weak, strong identity + number, forward parsing, filing log written once per change.

## D883. Whose court it is: teammate replies stop counting against you; status follows the court (#335, 2026-10-13)

`CommThread.court` ({owner: me | teammate | customer | nobody, source: rule | ai | override, basis, promise?}) is recomputed on
every new message. Rules: the last message from the customer → **me**; from me → **customer**; from a **teammate** →
**customer** (the fix: it no longer counts against the mailbox owner) — except, since D894, a teammate's **internal note**
(To/Cc with no outside address: → **me**, or **nobody** on a sign-off/FYI) and a teammate's reply whose own text **names
the owner** ("Jeff will call you" → **me**); a customer message that is only a sign-off ("thanks",
"got it", "sounds good", ≤ ~8 words, no question mark) → **nobody**. **Forwards:** a teammate forwarding to me is a hand-off
(court **me**), unless the note is FYI-only (court **nobody**, filed and archived on the original sender); my own forward out
to a vendor never moves the customer thread's court; the forwarded original is parsed outermost-external-first (Gmail and
Outlook formats), and a forward block in a later reply counts as `Fwd:`, not every reply in a thread that began as one.
**Internal-only threads** (every participant a Peak user or on Peak's own domain) are never noise, are filed only by a
number or a customer mention (otherwise `skipped`, no nagging), and follow the same rules between teammates. `status` keeps
its old meaning and is kept in step: me ↔ `waiting_us`, customer/teammate ↔ `waiting_them`, nobody ↔ `closed`; a manual
Mark replied/Close is kept until new mail, and a backlog run never reopens one. The pipeline's own writes
(`setStatus`/`archive`/`unarchive`/`setLink`) take **`{quiet}`**, so organizing never bumps `updatedAt` or reorders the inbox.
Morning triage's email feed reads the court (`me`) instead of raw `waiting_us`, and also requires the status to agree and the
thread not to be flagged noise, because a court can go stale (D893). "Not on me" / "On me" in the reader set
`source: "override"` by compare-and-set; it sticks until the next message. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` court checks — teammate reply → customer/`waiting_them`, sign-off → closed, teammate
forward → me filed on the original sender, FYI forward → nobody, customer forward, internal-only, override sticks then ends,
and the triage feed's court selection.

## D884. Archive-on-reply for everyone; outbound never un-archives; Mark replied / Close archive (#335, 2026-10-13)

When I reply (`comms.reply`, so also reply-all and forward) or a teammate's reply arrives that leaves the court on the
customer or nobody (never a teammate's internal note to me or a reply naming me — D894), the thread is archived in the app and in Gmail (`pushInboxState`) — for **every** user, not only
pilots. It is **filed first** when it already has a link or a strong suggestion (`filedBy: "reply"`, or `"teammate-reply"`);
a weak or missing suggestion waits in To file (stamped `archivedOnReply`, D889). Settings → Account **"Keep threads in my
inbox after I reply"** (`keepInInbox` in the user's notification prefs, default off = archive-on-reply on) turns it off per
user; with it on, a teammate's reply still never brings back a thread the owner had archived (it is re-archived quietly).
**`addMessage` no longer un-archives on an outbound message** — that covers app replies, sent drafts and logged outbound
calls/meetings; inbound mail (and inbound logged calls) still un-archive, and any message that makes the court **me**
un-archives. **Mark replied** and **Close** (`setStatusAction`) now archive too, honouring Keep, and ignore the court (after a
manual change the court is still "me"). The post-reply step runs in `after()` (`comms.reply(…, {postReply: "caller"})`); a
queued reply gets it when `flushOutbox` delivers it. A reply sent from Gmail itself (imported) does not archive-on-reply. A
strong suggestion for a different customer than the thread's hand link is ignored and the hand link is filed instead; a
foreign link is cleared and recorded so Undo restores it. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` apply checks — reply archives and files, keep-in-inbox, teammate reply archives and
doesn't count against me, hand-off un-archives, outbound call doesn't un-archive, queued reply via `flushOutbox`, Mark
replied/Close archive.

## D885. Noise: moved for pilots, tag-only for everyone else, never on a weak domain or an internal sender (#335, 2026-10-13)

Noise rules: Gmail `CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS|SOCIAL|FORUMS`, `List-Unsubscribe` or `Precedence: bulk|list` (the import now stores
`bulk`/`autoSubmitted` per message), a `no-?reply|notifications?|mailer-daemon|bounce` local part, an `Auto-Submitted`
header other than `no`, an out-of-office subject. **Never noise:** a known contact, an internal sender, an internal-only
thread, a thread the owner has written in (role check, so the owner's own address imported as inbound counts), a rescued
thread, and a sender rule `never-noise`. A **pilot** owner's noise is **moved** (`noise.moved`, archived, in the Noise tab);
anyone else gets the tag "Looks like noise" only. Noise on a thread whose only identity is a **weak domain guess** is
tag-only even for a pilot, and keeps the guess. AI noise moves only when the model says strong **and** no customer was
matched or guessed. A **manual Noise click moves the thread for everyone** (an explicit choice; the filing becomes
`dismissed`). **Not noise** sets `rescued`, un-archives, recomputes the filing, and offers a "never noise" rule; the AI
filing never makes a rescued thread noise again, and filing a flagged thread clears the flag. The Noise tab is every
flagged, unrescued thread I own, moved or still in the inbox ("Archive all shown" archives the tagged ones). Punch item
#335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — pilot noise moved/archived/quiet, non-pilot tag-only, weak-domain tag-only, known
contact and internal sender exempt, rescued stays rescued, filing clears the flag.

## D886. AI filing and AI court/promise reading are two Assist features on Haiku: `file` and `promise` (#335, 2026-10-13)

`AssistFeature` gains `file` (Haiku picks a filing target) and `promise` (Haiku reads the court and promises); each has its
own switch on the Assist pilot card (**Inbox organization**, **Promise tasks**; off until an admin turns them on — D897), a model env
var (`ASSIST_MODEL_FILE`, `ASSIST_MODEL_PROMISE`, both default `claude-haiku-5-5`), a 600/hour rate limit and a report row;
`isOrgPilot` is the one pilot check. **Filing** runs only when the rules left a thread unresolved or weak. The model sees
the thread in the untrusted wrapper plus a **server-built candidate list** (`id | type | label | customer`: the likely
customer's draft/sent quotes, non-done projects and open leads, newest 15, plus the top 5 company matches); any id outside
the list is discarded, and a result is **strong only when the model says so and the target is the matched customer or one of
its records**. `needsReply` = the model's flag AND the court is me. **Court reading** runs on the newest message unless it is a
pure sign-off, sees the last 3 messages and a server-verified who-wrote-each-message list, and overrides the rule court only
for a hand-off to "me" or a named real teammate; unknown ids are dropped, a teammate equal to the owner becomes me. No
model call on backlog mail, for a non-pilot owner, with no key, at the cap, or on a refusal — the pipeline stops after the
free rules. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` and `scripts/test-assist.ts` (feature defaults, models, rate limits, report rows) with
a fake provider — strong/weak, out-of-list id dropped, hand-off to a named teammate, unknown name dropped.

## D887. The AI pass runs after the response, is leased, and reads live court work first; the cron runs none (#335, 2026-10-13)

Rows needing AI carry `pendingAi` (filing and court). `runAiPass` runs **once per poll**, for the owners that poll synced, and
**never inside the request**: `sendReceiveAction` and `autoSyncAction` sync with `aiPass: false` and call the pass in
`after()` (Inbox page `maxDuration` 300) with a hard deadline of the action's start + 240 s. A call starts only inside the
~20 s window **and** with its worst case (30 s; 60 s when a local provider can fall back to Claude) plus 5 s left before
the deadline, so a pass is bounded at about 50 s. Concurrency: before each call the pass stamps `aiLeaseUntil` (now + 2 min)
by compare-and-set on the court and on the filing, every later write compares against what it last wrote (new mail or
another pass makes a stale result drop), and **`court.promisesFor = messageId` is written by compare-and-set before any task
is created**, so two passes make one task. Trade-off accepted: a process killed between the marker and the task writes drops
those tasks instead of duplicating them. The queue is **per owner** (SQL-filtered, so one user's 400 backlog rows can't
starve another), **court reads before filing**, oldest first; failed calls count an attempt (gives up at 3), a pre-call
refusal (cap, rate limit) skips the owner for the pass without one, stuck rows nobody can own are swept (50 per pass, at
most once an hour per process; the pass returns at once when no owner in its list is a pilot — D895), and
a stale-basis row is re-organized first and treated as backlog when its newest message is over 7 days old. **The
`/api/gmail/sync` cron runs no AI pass** (`aiPass: false`: a call needs ~35 s and the cron's 60 s is already shared by the
40 s import budget); on Vercel the server timer passes `aiPass: !process.env.VERCEL`. AI work therefore happens on Inbox ticks
and Send/Receive. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — the deadline (no call under 35 s left; fallback doubles it), budget window and
resume, two concurrent passes → one call and one task, live and expired leases, an exception counts an attempt, 400 backlog
rows don't starve another user, source pins that both actions use `after()` and the cron/timer pass `aiPass: false`.

## D888. Promise-tasks: deterministic id, due-date rules, owner/teammate only, under 7 days, never backlog (#335, 2026-10-13)

When the court reading returns promises on a message **I or a teammate sent** (or a forward note addressed to me), a task
is created through `createTaskOnce` with section `Email`, the thread/customer/site links, and the quote/project/lead
from the filing **only when it is filed or strong** (else the thread's own links), `notes: "From email: …"`, tier normal,
not `waitingOn`. **Id** `T-prm-<hash(threadId, messageId, promiseText)>`, so a re-sync never duplicates. **Owner:** the named
real team member (only when the newest message's own text names them — D899); else, for "we will…"/"someone will…", the message author if internal; else the thread owner; the creator
is the promise owner. **Due** (pure `resolveDue`, America/Chicago, 5:00 pm like the task calendar): today, tomorrow, a
weekday name (next occurrence, by text order), end of week → Friday, next week → next Monday, end of month, an explicit
date; otherwise 2 business days after the message. **Never** from a customer's own "we will…", **never** for mail older than 7
days (`PROMISE_MAX_AGE_MS`, a second guard behind backlog), never on the 90-day cleanup (D892). The reader shows "Task
created: … · due Thu" with **Undo** (soft-deletes the task, drops `court.promise`, logs `discarded`; shown only while the
task is open), and the composer offers an **unticked** "Mark '…' done?" — tasks are never auto-closed. Open: `court.promise`
holds only the first of up to 3 promises (all 3 tasks are created). Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — `resolveDue` for every phrase and the 2-business-day-5-pm default across a weekend,
deterministic ids, idempotent creation, owner resolution, a customer's "we will" makes none, mail over 7 days makes none,
Undo, the composer checkbox.

## D889. Sender rules, the To file scope, and what Undo restores (#335, 2026-10-13)

Corrections offer a rule — "Always file mail from this sender / @domain under X", "Never / Always treat as noise" — stored in
the `inbox_sender_rules` blob (cap 2,000; user beats company, email beats domain; company-wide needs `manage_users` and
refuses public domains, own domains and internal addresses). **Accepting a "file under X" rule sweeps** that sender's threads:
it **auto-files (link + archive unless a reply is owed, `filedBy: "rule"`) only the person's own threads that have no
customer or already carry the rule's customer** (a foreign-customer link is cleared, recorded for Undo); hand-linked threads
and other people's threads under a company rule only get a strong **suggestion**; a rule's `work` never replaces a
hand-picked work link on the same customer. The sweep covers inbox threads plus archived To file rows, at most 200 threads
and ~20 s, and a `skipped` thread of the person's own is reset to `suggested` first. **To file** is the person's non-deleted,
non-draft threads with a `suggested`, non-noise filing that are **in the inbox, or were archived by archive-on-reply without
filing** (`Filing.archivedOnReply`, cleared on filing, on un-archive and on new inbound mail, put back by Undo) — a thread
archived by hand or in Gmail never appears. **Undo** restores only what filing changed (`filing.applied`: customer identity
fields, work link, venue, archive, `archivedOnReply`), each part only while it is still the value filing set, and returns the
thread to `suggested`. `approveAllStrong` (capped at 500 / 20 s) requires a To file, strong row. Settings → Account lists and
deletes my own rules; the Assist pilot card has the admin company list. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — precedence, rule sweep (own / same-customer / hand-linked / other person's /
archived skipped), the To file scope (Gmail-archived and hand-archived excluded, archived-on-reply included), Undo restoring
each part, approve-all on strong rows only, rule delete authorization.

## D890. Logging: auto-filings never set an AI outcome; the report counts them apart (#335, 2026-10-13)

AI filings are logged in `assist_runs` (`file` runs). A human action sets the outcome — Approve `accepted`, Change/Not noise
`edited`, Skip `discarded`, first write wins; Undo notes `undone` in the detail. A filing nobody decided (on reply, teammate
reply, sender rule) records **`outcomeDetail.autoFiled`** (`reply` | `teammate-reply` | `rule`) and **leaves the outcome
null**, so "% approved" isn't inflated. Rule/identity/number/noise-rule filings go to the capped `inbox_filing_log` (2,000)
with an `action`. The Assist pilot card's report (`filingReport`, pure) has a row per source with suggested, approved,
corrected, rescued, skipped, undone and auto-filed, **% approved = approved ÷ (approved + corrected + rescued + skipped)**
(auto-filed excluded), court overrides, and promise-tasks created/undone (`T-prm-%` tasks, deleted = undone), for the chosen
month. The 90-day cleanup's rule suggestions are counted in its own state blob, not the log (D892), and shown as a
separate "From 'Organize my inbox': N suggested (by source)" line under the table. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — report math and AI/log mapping, an empty month, `autoFiled` leaves the outcome null,
`cleanupRuleSuggestions` sums the state blobs of runs started in the month.

## D891. Peak's own domain: an admin override replaces the derived domains; Peak's domain is always kept; freemail refused (#335, 2026-10-13)

"Internal" means a Peak user (team list, users' emails, connected Gmail addresses) or an address on Peak's own domain.
`ownDomainsFrom` = `peaksystemsgroup.com` (**always**, subdomains included — the shared `isPeakAddress` check) plus **either**
the admin override on the Assist pilot card **or**, with no valid override, the team's non-freemail domains. An override
**replaces** the derived domains, it doesn't add to them. A public mail provider (`FREEMAIL_DOMAINS`) is refused by
`setOwnDomainOverrideAction` ("… can't be Peak's own domain"). The organization context is cached 60 s per process;
every settings change (pilot list, feature switches, override, key save/remove, an accepted rule) calls
`invalidateOrgContext()`. The pipeline and `inbox-identity.ts` use the same Peak domain. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — override replaces derived, Peak domain kept under any override, a freemail override
leaves Peak's domain only, an empty team still gives Peak's domain, pipeline and identity agree.

## D892. "Organize my inbox": a suggest-only 90-day cleanup, and the one-time filing-basis recompute (#335, 2026-10-13)

Pilot users get an **Organize my inbox** button (Organize header) that walks their personal, live, in-inbox email threads last
active within 90 days (newest email, capped at 5,000), not filed or dismissed, newest first, in resumable batches of 40 s
(state blob `inbox_cleanup:<userId>`, the id list fixed at start, "212 of 480 checked", a lease against a second tab, a new
run when the last finished or went a day stale). **It only suggests:** nothing is linked or archived (the one archive is a
pilot's noise moving to the Noise tab), rules run as **backlog** — court rules only, **no promise-tasks and no court
reading**, and a backlog organize **keeps a live court's `pendingAi`/lease/`promisesFor`/`promise` exactly as it is**
(`filingOnly` AI pass; live court AI work from a sync isn't lost). The rules phase stops 15 s early and the rest of the budget
goes to the filing AI; what doesn't fit resumes on later passes ("still with AI"). It is **not logged per entry**: the mass
rule suggestions are counted by source in the state blob (`ruleSuggestions`) so they can't evict the 2,000-entry filing log;
decisions on them are logged as usual. A re-run is a no-op on already-suggested threads (the pipeline keeps the same
record). **One-time recompute:** a filing's `basis` was the newest message id; it is now the **newest outside message**
(`filingBasisMessage`), so my own or a teammate's reply never resets a pending suggestion. Filings written before this carry
the old basis, so the first organize of each such thread recomputes it once (the court keeps its newest-message basis).
Internal-only threads use their newest message, and a teammate's forward of outside mail also re-bases. Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` — pilot-only, resumable across two batches, suggest-only, no tasks with a
promise-reading fake model, a live court's `pendingAi` deep-equal after a batch, the summary, the lease, own replies keep a
pending/skipped filing, new outside mail resets it.

## D893. Follow-up risks accepted at ship; gates (#335, 2026-10-13)

(1) **`recordMessage` appends with a whole-doc `patchDoc`** (the pipeline's own quiet archive / unarchive / setStatus no
longer do — they are key-level since D896), so an org key (`filing`, `court`, `noise`) written by a
concurrent AI pass or an apply action in that window can be clobbered; org writes themselves are key-level (`setOrg`,
compare-and-set where it matters) and the pipeline self-heals a missing filing/court/noise on the next organize. The fix is an
atomic append. (2) `setOrg` filing writes are last-write-wins, so an organize racing an Approve can overwrite `filed` in a
small window. (3) A court can go stale when a status changes without a re-organize (in-app replies, Mark replied, Gmail status
labels), which is why triage also checks `status`. (4) `autoSyncAction`'s inline `flushOutbox` still runs the post-reply
step on the request path when it delivers offline-queued mail. (5) The AI pass scans `comms` by jsonb `pendingAi`, unindexed.
(6) The cron runs no AI pass (D887). (7) `court.promise` keeps only the first of 3 promises (D888). (8) My own forward out
re-bases a suggested filing, which can replace a kept AI suggestion. (9) Undo doesn't restore a cleared noise
flag. No migration (the org fields ride the comms doc; `inbox_sender_rules`, `inbox_filing_log`, `inbox_cleanup:<userId>`
and the own-domain override are blobs). Punch item #335.

## D894. A teammate's internal note never archives a customer thread; a reply naming the owner is a rule hand-off (#335, 2026-10-13)

Final review found that court rule 4 looked only at the sender: a teammate's note to the owner alone on a customer thread
("Jeff, can you take this, they want pricing Friday"), or one cc'ing the owner as a hand-off, made the court **customer**,
and `afterImportedMessage` then archived the thread in the app and in Gmail for every user. `CourtMessage` now carries the
message's **To/Cc** (the pipeline passes `addressesIn(m.to/cc)`), and a teammate's last message (a shared Peak address counts
as a teammate) reads: **To/Cc with no outside address** = an internal note the customer never saw → a pure sign-off or an FYI
note (`isFyiNote`, now exported) → **nobody**; anything else → **me** (addressed to me, a question, my name, or just a note I
was sent — the safe side is never archiving on a guess). **To the customer, with the owner's first or full name in its own
text** (`ownText`, quoted reply and signature stripped) → **me** ("Jeff will be in touch tomorrow" — a rule-level hand-off,
for everyone, no AI). Otherwise → **customer** as before; a message with no recorded To/Cc is read as a reply to the
customer. Names come from the team list's display name (`src/lib/inbox-org/names.ts`): name words only (a token with digits
such as `TEST335` is skipped), case-insensitive and word-bounded — except a first name that is an everyday word (Will, Mark,
Grant, May…) matches only capitalised, so "I will call" never names Will. **What each layer catches:** the rules catch an
internal note and a hand-off that names the owner; the AI reading (pilot only) still catches a hand-off to another teammate
and one phrased without the owner's name ("our account lead will send pricing"). Punch item #335.
Verified: `scripts/test-inbox-org.ts` court checks (note to the owner only → me; cc'd internal note → me; internal sign-off
/ FYI → nobody; "Jeff will be in touch" to the customer → me; full name; a name only in the quoted text doesn't count;
plain reply → customer; everyday-word names; a shared address both ways) and imported-mail checks through `recordMessage`
(a teammate's note to me → court me, not archived; it brings an archived thread back; "Ann will be in touch" → me by rule
for a non-pilot owner).

## D895. The AI pass does nothing unless an owner in its list is a pilot; the stuck-row sweep runs hourly (#335, 2026-10-13)

`scheduleAiPass` runs on every Inbox tick, so `runAiPass` returns before any query unless at least one owner in its list
passes `isOrgPilot(owner, "file" | "promise")` (a pilot user with both switches off counts as no pilot). The sweep that
clears pending rows nobody can own (an unindexed jsonb scan) runs only when the pass got that far and at most once an hour
per process (a module timestamp; `resetAiPassSweep()` for the checks). Trade-off: rows left pending for an owner who later
leaves the pilot stay marked until a pilot's pass reaches them or the owner rejoins — harmless, the rules already ran.
Verified: no pilot → `looked 0`, nothing cleared, no call; a gated-off owner beside a pilot still gets pending cleared; a
second pass within the hour doesn't sweep, one an hour later does.

## D896. The pipeline's quiet archive / unarchive / setStatus write one key (#335, 2026-10-13)

`comms.archive` / `unarchive` / `setStatus` with `{quiet: true}` (every pipeline, AI-pass and apply path) write only
`archived` / `status` with `patchDocKey` (in-SQL `doc || {key: value}`), never a read-modify-write of the whole doc, so a
message the Gmail import appends meanwhile can no longer be lost. A quiet unarchive drops `filing.archivedOnReply` by
compare-and-set on the `filing` key (re-read and retried up to 3 times). A quiet `setStatus` with an unknown status writes
nothing. `dispatchInboxState` / `queuePeakLabelSync` run exactly as before; a person's (non-quiet) archive / status change
still touches the doc as before. `pushInboxState` stamps `gmailInboxed` key-level too (`setGmailInboxed`). Still open (D893):
`recordMessage`'s own append is a whole-doc write, so two appends to one thread at once can clobber each other — one
mailbox's imports run one after another, so this needs an atomic append, not this fix.
Verified: imports racing repeated quiet archive / unarchive / setStatus keep every message (the same check fails with the
old whole-doc write), plus source pins.

`assistSettingsOf` reads the `file` and `promise` features as on only when stored `=== true` (`OPT_IN_FEATURES`); tasks /

## D898. Moving a thread back to the Gmail inbox brings it back in the app (#335, 2026-10-13)

`reconcileInboxState` now treats an explicit `gmailInboxed` false → true flip (the person moved the thread back to INBOX in
Gmail) as "bring it back": `reinboxFromGmail` sets `gmailInboxed` true, `archived` false and clears
`filing.archivedOnReply`, all key-level, with no push back to Gmail. Pipeline-moved noise brought back this way counts as
**rescued** (like Not noise), so the next organize doesn't move it out again. Before this, a thread archived on reply and
re-inboxed in Gmail stayed hidden in the app (`archived` stayed true). Known race, accepted: an app archive whose Gmail push
lands between the reconcile's `in:inbox` listing and its read of the threads can be undone; the next reconcile sees it out
of the inbox and the person archives it again.

## D899. A promise-task goes to the person the newest message names, never to a name the model was steered to (#335, 2026-10-13)

thread can no longer route a task to someone the Peak author didn't name. Supersedes D888's "the named real team member".
Verified: a model owner named only in quoted text → the internal author; no author → the thread owner; an unnamed AI
hand-off's promise → the author.

A court not computed against the thread's newest email message (`court.basis` ≠ that id; no basis → judged by time; `src/lib/inbox-org/court-current.ts`) is stale — organizing failed, or `INBOX_ORG_DISABLED` is on — and must not hide new customer mail. `onMyCourt` (Morning triage's email feed) then decides by status alone, and with the kill switch on reads only the status (court and noise tag ignored). `rederiveStatuses` (Gmail bridge) keeps a court-driven status only while the court is current; under a stale court it re-derives the status as before #335. ## D902. Pop-outs are named browser windows opening the same pages (#336, 2026-10-13)

Approach A from the brainstorm: a pop-out is the ordinary page opened in a browser window named `peak-pop:<kind>:<id>` (`inbox:box`, `thread:<id>`, `estimate:<id>`, `customer:<id>`; the nav uses `list` / `new` as the id). No separate routes, no second layout. One window per item: popping out the same item again focuses its window. The kinds, names, features and URL rules are pure (`src/lib/popout/`: `names.ts`, `geometry.ts`, `channel.ts`, `guard.ts`, `click.ts`, `live.ts`, `open.ts`), and `window.name` is the only state that makes a window a pop-out, so navigating inside one stays a pop-out. Everything is client-side: no migration, no env var, no server flag, and so no kill switch to document (turn it off by removing the ⧉ buttons; the head script only reads `window.name`). Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-popout-windows-design.md`.

## D903. The pop-out class comes from a head script, and the CSS does the rest (#336, 2026-10-13)

A plain inline `<script>` in the root layout's `<head>` (`POP_HEAD_SCRIPT` in `live.ts`) adds `pk-pop` to `<html>` when `window.name` starts with `peak-pop:`. It reads nothing else, touches no storage or network, and sits in try/catch. It is a raw script, not `next/script` `beforeInteractive`, because the Next 16 docs' own pre-hydration pattern is the inline head script, which runs synchronously before first paint; `beforeInteractive` is preloaded but does not promise to run before paint, so the nav could flash. `<html>` gained `suppressHydrationWarning` for it, and `LiveSync` re-applies the class in a layout effect because dev Strict Mode resets `<html>` attributes on remount. `globals.css`: `html.pk-pop .pk-nav` is hidden, `.pk-shell` is one column and `.pk-main` is full width; `.pk-pop-header` shows only in pop-out mode and is hidden in print. The ⧉ affordances (`.pk-popout-affordance`) are hidden below 900 px and in the native shell (`html.pk-native`, set from the existing Capacitor check in `src/lib/platform.ts`), where a pop-up window makes no sense. The pop-out header shows the page title (`document.title` less the " — Quartzite-6" suffix, kept current by an observer that exists only in pop-out mode), **Open in main window** and ✕.

## D904. Opening is `window.open("", name)`, then a location replace; it returns a boolean (#336, 2026-10-13)

`openPopout(kind, id, url)` calls `window.open("", name, features)` with an empty URL. A brand-new window comes back as `about:blank` and is sent to the URL with `location.replace`; an existing window of that name is only focused and is never reloaded, so unsaved typing in it survives. The spec and brief said `window.open(url, name, …)`; that navigates an existing window of the same name, which reloads it and would break both "popping out the same item focuses its window" and "unsaved typing is never overwritten". It returns `true` when the window opened or was focused and `false` when the browser blocked it (a notice says "Your browser blocked the window — allow pop-ups for this site."); the spec said `void`, but `PopoutButton` uses the boolean to run `onOpen`, for example to close the nav dropdown. Plain clicks and cmd/ctrl-clicks are untouched; shift-click on email rows, estimate rows (Quotes hub, customer record quote lists, Home pipeline cards and stage sheet) and the Companies directory rows pops out.

## D905. Window size and position are remembered per screen type, as inner size (#336, 2026-10-13)

A pop-out saves `{left: screenX, top: screenY, width: innerWidth, height: innerHeight}` under its kind in `localStorage`, and `openPopout` reads it back as the `window.open` features. `width`/`height` in `window.open` features are the inner (content) size, so saving the outer frame grew the window by its chrome on every reopen; inner size round-trips exactly (pinned: save → reopen → save keeps the size). Defaults: estimate 1100×800, customer 900×800, thread and inbox 760×800, centred on the opener's screen. Saved sizes are floored at 320×240, capped to the screen, and a negative origin (a second monitor on the left) is kept. Storage that throws just means defaults.

## D906. Window ids are `{id, name}`; the most recently focused main window answers "Open in main window" (#336, 2026-10-13)

Each window mints a random id (`peak-window-id` in `sessionStorage`, stored as `{id, name}`), re-minted when the stored name differs from `window.name`, so a window renamed by being popped out never shares its opener's id (a duplicated unnamed tab does share one, documented). The id lets a window ignore its own broadcasts. "Open in main window" posts `open-in-main` on the `BroadcastChannel("peak")` channel; only the most recently focused main window (a window without `pk-pop`) answers, with an ack, then calls `window.focus()` and `router.push`es the same-origin path (`toAppPath` refuses anything off-origin). `window.focus()` is limited by browsers: Chrome and Firefox may only flash the tab, and Safari may not move it. If no ack arrives within 500 ms the pop-out opens the URL in a new tab, which Safari can block as a pop-up because it is not in the click's gesture any more.

## D907. LiveSync: debounce, typing guard, 30 s focus refresh, self-ignore (#336, 2026-10-13)

One `LiveSync` client component mounted once in `(app)/layout.tsx` (it replaces the #335 `InboxChangedListener`, which is deleted along with its three mounts). Another window's `changed` message `{entity, id}` makes this window owe a refresh. Every window refreshes on any `changed`, whatever it is showing; there is no per-item filter. The refresh is `router.refresh()` armed 1 s after the message (at most one per 5 s, D911) and then run through the typing guard (D913): it waits while an editable field (text input, textarea, contenteditable; not read-only or disabled) is focused, and until 3 s after the last capture-phase `keydown` on one. When a window regains focus or visibility it refreshes only if the last refresh is over 30 s old, after a 1.5 s settle (D910); mount and every **pathname** change count as a refresh, so the first focus does not refetch. A change of search params alone (`?thread=`, `?step=`) does not count. Neither kind of refresh runs offline (D910), and a page's unsaved-work hold skips the focus refresh (D912). A window ignores messages carrying its own id. The legacy `inbox-changed` message is still delivered, as a `changed`/`thread`. Because the refresh is a server re-render, the estimator's store-owned `bonusRecord` and similar fields come back on it; nothing is merged client-side.

## D908. Posters: which saves broadcast, and what is left to the focus refresh (#336, 2026-10-13)

Client code posts `postChanged(entity, id)` from `src/lib/popout/channel.ts` after an awaited action succeeds; no server-action signature changed. Estimator (`quote`): Save, status, stage, pipeline, meta, package selection, people, bonus split, alternates, move/copy system (the target id), the next-step control (shared by the Estimator toolbar, Quotes hub and phone preview), review sidebar, comment pins, send composer and activity (`thread`), the package staff panel, client link and the portal Decline. Customer record (`customer`): company edit/delete, venue dialog, notes, portal access, logo, people, documents. Tasks (`task`, plus `thread` where tied to one): the Inbox task dialogs and cards, the queue, the calendar chip/popover/At risk panel, and `TasksCard` (add, remove, chips, and, from the follow-up, the status and assignee/due selects, whose `<form action>` is wrapped so it posts after the write and `requestSubmit` still works). Left to the 30 s focus refresh because a bare `<form action={serverAction}>` has no client result to hook without changing a signature: the Quotes-hub `setQuoteStatus` and the default `PortalPanel` Approve. Also not posting: the Portal quotes queue, the Organize and Meetings lists, and other customer cross-links.

## D909. The nav ⧉ and the known limits (#336, 2026-10-13)

The nav shows a hover ⧉ beside Inbox, Estimator and Customers (`NAV_POPOUT`); the Customers tab is a dropdown with no page of its own, so its ⧉ sits on the **Companies** row and opens `customer:list` at `/companies`; in the collapsed sidebar rail the ⧉ stacks under the toggle. Known limits, all browser behaviour left alone: a browser finds a window by name only among windows its opener knows, so a pop-out opened from main tab A is not found from main tab B (B opens a second window with the same name), and the same can happen after the opener reloads or after an SSO redirect or a cross-origin-opener-policy response severs the link; the new-tab fallback in D906 can be blocked in Safari. Punch item #336.

## D910. LiveSync never refreshes offline (#336 final review, 2026-10-13)

In Next 16.3.5 a `router.refresh()` whose fetch fails falls back to a full browser reload (`ppr-navigations.js`; `experimental.useOffline` is off). The service worker (`public/sw.js`) then answers with cached or offline HTML and every in-memory edit is gone. A laptop that wakes before Wi-Fi is back fires focus/visibility first, so the old immediate focus refresh hit exactly this. Now every owed refresh goes through `nextRefreshStep` (`src/lib/popout/guard.ts`), which parks it (`offline`) when `navigator.onLine` is false or the sync engine reports `connected: false` (`getEngine().getStatus()`, which is also false under **Work offline**). A parked refresh runs 2 s after the window `online` event or the engine's `peak-sync` event reports connected again, or on the next change/focus that finds the network back. Focus and visibility refreshes wait 1.5 s first, and the gate is checked when the timer fires, not when the event arrives. An unknown state (no `navigator`) does not block. Pure gate: `canRefreshOnline`.

## D911. Change-driven refreshes are trailing-throttled to one per 5 s (#336 final review, 2026-10-13)

The Estimator autosaves its note, assumptions, cover summary and Not included 500 ms after each pause, and each autosave posts `quote`, so other windows refreshed about every 1.5 s while someone typed. A `changed` message now arms its timer at `max(1 s, 5 s − time since the last refresh)` (`changeDelayMs`), and `nextRefreshStep` re-checks the 5 s gap (`throttleWaitMs`) when it fires. A message that arrives while a timer is already pending leaves that timer alone: the refresh it runs fetches every save made so far, so the last change is always honoured. A navigation counts as a refresh for the throttle. Focus refreshes are not throttled (they have their own 30 s rule).

## D912. The unsaved-work hold, and Open in main window never discards work (#336 final review, 2026-10-13)

`setUnsavedHold(on)` / `hasUnsavedHold()` (`src/lib/popout/hold.ts`, client module state, no imports) let a page say it holds unsaved work. The Estimator sets it from `pdfDirty || (no id yet && any system has lines)` in an effect keyed on that boolean, and clears it on unmount. `pdfDirty` stays true after a text autosave until the next Save, so the hold errs on the side of keeping work. While the hold is on, LiveSync drops the focus refresh; change-driven refreshes still run, because `router.refresh()` keeps client state. A main window does not answer **Open in main window** (`canYieldToOpenInMain`) while the hold is on, while an editable field is focused, or within 3 s of a keystroke in one. It stays silent, so after 500 ms the pop-out opens the page in a new tab instead of navigating the main window away from the work. No other page sets the hold yet.

## D913. The typing guard is OR, as the spec says (#336 final review, 2026-10-13)

D907 shipped with AND (defer only while a field is focused AND a key was pressed in the last 3 s). Spec §5 says OR. `shouldRefreshNow` now does this:
- **Change-driven refresh:** waits until 3 s after the last keystroke in an editable field, even if the field has since lost focus. It also waits while an editable field is focused, re-checking every 3 s.
- **Focus refresh:** waits only while an editable field is focused.
- "Focused" means focused in a window that has focus (`document.hasFocus() && isEditableTarget(activeElement)`, `editableBlocksRefresh`): a caret left in a background window's field does not block its refreshes; Open in main window still uses the raw caret (D912).

There is no reliable "unsaved input" signal for an arbitrary field, because React keeps a controlled input's `value` attribute in sync, so a focused editable field counts as unsaved. A person who leaves the cursor in a search box gets the refresh when they leave it.
Verified 2026-10-13 (D910–D913): see PUNCHLIST #336 "Final-review fixes".

## D914. Brief slots are 6:45 and 13:45; the crons are fixed UTC and the lazy build covers drift (AI daily brief, 2026-10-13)

`slotAt` (`src/lib/triage/clock.ts`) is minute-precise: at or after 13:45 Chicago is `midday`, otherwise `morning`; the stored names are unchanged (`MORNING_AT_MIN`, `MIDDAY_AT_MIN`, `minuteOfDay`). `vercel.json` runs `/api/gmail/sync` at `45 11 * * *` and `/api/triage/build?slot=midday` at `45 18 * * *`, which are 6:45 and 13:45 CDT. Vercel crons are UTC with no DST fix, so in winter they fire at 5:45 and 12:45 CST. The midday build passes its slot explicitly (`loadTriageView` takes `opts.at`) instead of asking `slotAt`, which would say morning at 12:45. The winter morning build happens before 6:45, and the first view after 6:45 builds lazily if it is missing. Before 6:45, `beforeMorning` shows yesterday's afternoon brief (marked `stale: "yesterday-afternoon"`, no Rebuild) or nothing, and never builds. The drive cron stays at `0 11`. The two triage pins in `test-morning-triage.ts` moved to 18:45 UTC and 13:44 → morning.

## D915. The brief is one blob per user and slot; writes insert if absent, Rebuild replaces, a malformed blob is replaced (2026-10-13)

`brief:<userId>:<day>:<slot>`, no migration. Cron and lazy builds write with `setBlobKeysIfAbsent` (atomic), so two builders never fight and the first one stands. Every key is written, with absent optional keys stored as `null`. Rebuild writes with `setBlob`, which replaces all keys and so clears a stale `error` or `since`. `briefFromBlob` accepts only a whole brief (string `userId`/`day`/`summary`, numeric `builtAt`, a valid slot, and well-formed `doFirst`, `organize`, `today`, `quiet`, `newPromiseTasks`, `approvals`, `since`). Anything else reads as missing, and the insert path replaces the blob whole when its read-back fails validation, so a bad blob cannot trigger a fresh model call on every view. If a build throws, the view gets an unstored minimal rule brief marked `transient`; a lazy build that only ran out of time is not stored either, and the cron may replace a stored lazy brief that carries an error (D928). The Home card needs the pilot, the Daily brief switch and Assist's key (D923); `loadBriefView` itself does not need the key, so a stored rule-built brief still reads.

## D916. The summary is Haiku, limited to snapshot keys, with a rule-built fallback (2026-10-13)

One Haiku call per brief (feature `brief`, `countRate: false`, `ASSIST_MODEL_BRIEF`). The prompt carries the facts and up to 40 rows (`key | source | title | reason`) inside one `<brief_data>` wrapper; every field is cleaned so it cannot carry `<`, `>`, `|` or the wrapper tag. `sanitizeBrief` keeps only `doFirst` keys that exist in the triage snapshot (3 to 5; the model can never invent a row or a link), caps the summary at 900 characters and strips markdown links and tags. A refusal, an unusable answer, no time left, a failed gate or a thrown `runAssist` gives `ruleBrief(facts)` (the same facts in plain words, "N tasks on today's plan") with `error` set. A model failure is stored and not retried on view, so a bad day costs one call per slot.

## D917. The AI-pass slice runs on Rebuild only, with a 90 s deadline (2026-10-13)

A brief build can first run `runAiPass` for that user (8 s window to start calls) so court and filing are fresh. That pass needs about 50 s of headroom (its own 35 s worst case plus the brief's 15 s reserve), so it is gated on `builtBy === "rebuild"` and never runs in the lazy (20 s) or cron (≤ 50 s) paths, where it would crowd out the summary. Rebuild is a Server Action on Home, and Home has `maxDuration = 120`, so `BRIEF_REBUILD_DEADLINE_MS` is 90 s. Rebuild is limited to 3 per hour per user (`rateLimit`, refused tries do not count); the limit is per process (a follow-up on PUNCHLIST #337).

## D918. The draft queue: Sonnet for replies, Haiku for tasks and nudges, bounded by the cap and a deadline (2026-10-13)

`runDraftQueue` (`src/lib/brief/drafts.ts`) is the Daily brief's: it runs only for a pilot user with the **Daily brief** switch on (`briefOnFor`; the switch is opt-in, default off, as the spec says), and Reply, Task suggestions and the nudges then each need their own feature on (Reply and Task suggestions default on, so a pilot user without Daily brief gets no background drafting at all, from Home, the Inbox or the crons). For such a user it pre-drafts every email thread the Organize sweep puts on their court (oldest wait first; assigned to them, visible, not archived or deleted, has inbound mail), then nudges for quiet quotes. Per thread: a reply (Sonnet, feature `reply`) and task suggestions (Haiku, feature `tasks`), stored as one `CommThread.preDraft`. The calls run with `countRate: false`, so the interactive per-hour rate limit (`RATE_LIMITS` reply and tasks: 60 per hour) never starves a person; the monthly cap bounds them, a cap refusal stops the queue, and the queue pauses on its own at 60 % of the cap (D927). Each call is capped to the time left (`maxRetries` 0, half the time when a fallback provider exists) and no call starts with under 15 s left. Cheap gate first: it reads only settings and env and returns before any other query unless the owner is pilot with Daily brief on and a relevant feature usable; the month's spend (D927) is the next read. In-process guards allow one queue per owner at a time and a 60 s gap between runs. An unusable answer is stored as `replyError`/`tasksError`/`error` and retried after 6 h (`DRAFT_RETRY_MS`).

## D919. Leases and basis-checked writes keep drafts from racing (2026-10-13)

Two serverless instances can run the queue at once, so each thread has `preDraftLeaseUntil` and each quote `assistNudgeLeaseUntil` (the ai-pass `aiLeaseUntil` pattern: a separate top-level key, taken by compare-and-set on the value read, held until the deadline plus 30 s, released in `finally`; `Quote.update()` drops the quote key). Before drafting, the queue re-reads the doc and re-checks court and freshness (for a quote: still sent, same send). After the call it re-reads again and writes only when the basis is unchanged and only by compare-and-set over the value read under the lease; otherwise the result counts `dropped`. New mail arriving mid-call drops the older reply. The writes are key-level (`patchDocKey`, `casDocKey`), so a quote's `estNo`, `estSuffix` and `updatedAt` (the approval and send version) are untouched. Known gap: comms whole-doc writers (`patchDoc`, the Gmail import) can still erase a lease or pre-draft that lands between their read and write; the worst case is one duplicate call (PUNCHLIST #337).

## D920. Where the queue runs: Home and Inbox `after()`, then the cron riders (2026-10-13)

Home runs the owner's queue in `after()` with a 110 s deadline (Home's `maxDuration` is 120). The Inbox runs it for the signed-in user in `scheduleAiPass`'s `after()`, right after `runAiPass`; with `INBOX_ORG_DISABLED` that function returns early and the Inbox schedules nothing, while Home still drafts. Either way the queue itself returns at once unless the user has Daily brief on (D918). The crons are riders: `/api/triage/build` builds that slot's briefs and then drafts for the built users, each in its own try, ending at 50 s (`BRIEF_DEADLINE_MS`; calls are capped 5 s before it, which leaves 10 s under the 60 s ceiling for the writes and the response). `/api/gmail/sync` runs, after the morning triage, the Krisp meeting sync first (`min(20 s, 35 s − elapsed)`, so meetings keep their window and are not starved by the briefs), then the morning briefs and drafts, both capped at 35 s (`BRIEF_CRON_CUTOFF_MS`), then the photo sync, which therefore still gets its 10 s minimum before its 45 s cutoff (its hard stop is budget + 10 s, so 55 s at worst). A Krisp call already in flight can run its own 20 s timeout past 35 s (55 s at worst); the briefs, drafts and photos then find no time and skip (briefs build lazily on Home, photos run the next day). The photo rider's 10 s is best-effort, not a guarantee: a slow brief gather or a long Krisp run can push the photo sync to the next day. A brief build starts only with at least 12 s left and a queue only with at least 20 s, so on a heavy morning the cron does less and Home does the rest. Every call is bounded by the monthly cap and logged in `assist_runs`.

## D921. Reusable `reply-server` and `tasks-server`, with per-call limits that can only shorten (2026-10-13)

`draftReplyForThread(threadId, me, deps)` and `suggestTasksForThread` (`src/lib/assist/reply-server.ts`, `tasks-server.ts`) hold what the two Server Actions used to do inline, behind the shared `gateFor` (`gate-server.ts`).
