The actions are thin wrappers that map failures (`gate`, `thread`, `model`, `deadline`) back to the old `{ ok, … }` shapes, so the manual buttons behave as before. `runAssist` gained `RunArgs.limits` (`CallLimits`): a per-call timeout and retry count that can only shorten the slot's values, via `capAt(slot, cap, floor)` (timeout at least 1 ms, retries at least 0, so 0 never falls back to the 60 s default). This was needed because a Sonnet reply's worst case under the slot settings is 60 s × 2 attempts, so no reply could ever start inside a 110 s window. `limitsBefore` (`call-budget.ts`) turns a deadline into limits after the function's own loads, and refuses with `deadline` when too little is left. The queue passes `preloaded` threads, quotes, signature and team so it loads each once per run.

## D922. Quiet quotes: the owner's, at least 5 business days old, no reply seen, at most 8 (2026-10-13)

`selectQuietQuotes` (`src/lib/brief/quiet.ts`, pure) lists a person's sent quotes that have gone quiet. Whose: the quote's `owner`, else `preparedBy` (`quoteIsMine`). Quiet: still `sent`, and the last history entry (the move to sent) is at least 5 business days old (`QUIET_BUSINESS_DAYS`, Chicago clock). A quote drops out when a linked thread has an inbound message after the send, or when an inbound subject carries its estimate number (token match). Oldest sent first, at most 8 (`QUIET_MAX`). Each gets a Haiku nudge stored as `Quote.assistNudge` `{ note, emailSubject, emailBody }`: the prompt wraps customer-written fields in `<quote_facts>`, includes the price only for a sent quote above $0, and `sanitizeNudge` caps lengths (note 300, subject 120, body 2000), strips the signature and refuses any dollar figure other than the sent value. A nudge is fresh only while the quote is still the same send.

## D923. The Home card: pilot and brief only, never breaks Home, and "Use it" only for a good pre-draft (2026-10-13)

The BriefCard sits above Start here, behind its own Suspense, and renders only for a pilot user with Daily brief on and Assist's key (D881) usable. All of its work happens inside one try/catch: any throw shows "Your brief couldn't load — Start here below still has your list." and Home renders anyway. The card shows the summary, Do these first (title and link read from the brief's own snapshot, never the raw key), the Organize line, promises, Today, approvals, quiet quotes and, in the afternoon, a "since this morning" line. Chips: **Draft ready** and **Tasks ready** per thread. In the reader, "Draft reply ready · prepared hh:mm · Use it" shows only for a fresh pre-draft that was made for the viewer (`PreDraft.ownerId`, D929), is assigned to the viewer, still on their court and has a non-empty body (`readerPreDraft`); Suggest tasks opens the stored suggestions only when there is at least one. Use it makes no model call. Parked-draft outcomes: closing the composer unsent parks the draft and records nothing; the next Use it on the same run re-attaches it; the eventual send records accepted or edited; it is recorded `discarded` only when the reader unmounts, or when a newer pre-draft replaces it; a run already sent from this reader is never re-attached. Each pre-draft run therefore gets exactly one outcome. Lead rows show "Ready to quote? → Open lead" (`/leads?lead=<id>`).

## D924. Send nudge travels by id; the recipient is resolved on the server (2026-10-13)

The card's Send nudge links to `/inbox?nudge=<quoteId>`. The Inbox page loads the quote and builds the prefill with `nudgePrefill(q, me)`, which returns null unless the nudge is fresh, was made for the viewer (`AssistNudge.ownerId`, D929), has no error, has a non-empty body, and the quote is the viewer's own (`quoteIsMine`). The card shows Send nudge only when that same rule would succeed. Subject (one line, 200), body (5000, control characters out) and contact (120) are capped in `inbox-compose-prefill.ts`; the body gets the viewer's signature server-side; To is the named contact matched by name among the customer's people, else blank. No subject, body or email address ever rides in the URL, and a plain `?new=` behaves exactly as before. Nothing sends: the person edits and presses Send in the composer.

## D925. Phone: a big-text view, Listen, and two local notifications (2026-10-13)

Under 900 px the card shows the summary, Do these first and the counts, with no drafts. Listen reads `speechSynthesis` with `briefSpeech` (links, tags and brackets stripped, "are on today's plan"); it is hidden where unsupported and cancelled on unmount. The collapse state is per brief id in `localStorage`, in try/catch. Reminders are Capacitor local notifications (`@capacitor/local-notifications` pinned exactly to 8.3.1) with fixed ids 64501 (morning) and 64502 (afternoon), repeating at 6:45 and 13:45 on the phone's clock, with generic text ("Your morning brief is ready") and target `/?brief=1`. They are scheduled by `NativeBriefReminders` in the `(app)` layout only on a native platform, with the plugin loaded by dynamic `import()` inside try/catch, so the web build and an app built before `cap sync` are unaffected: the import fails quietly and there are no reminders. Account gets **Brief reminders on this phone** (`brief_reminders`), on by default and shown only to pilot users with Daily brief. Turning it off cancels both ids. `npx cap sync` and a rebuild of the iOS and Android apps are left to Jeff; `Package.swift` is managed by Capacitor and not edited by hand.

## D926. The Assist report measures only what it can see (2026-10-13)

The Assist pilot card gains a Daily brief table (`briefReport`, `loadBriefBuilds`). Measured: briefs built by cron, lazy and rebuild (read from the brief blobs of the month's ids, at most 1,500 reads in chunks of 50); pre-drafts made, used (outcome accepted or edited), discarded and not used (no outcome), where made = used + discarded + not used; and nudges made (ok `brief` runs whose `contextRef` starts with `quote:`). Pre-drafts are counted from a `queued` marker the queue writes to the run detail when a reply lands (`report-keys.ts`), so live replies, failed runs, task runs and brief-build runs are excluded, and pre-drafts made before this change are not counted. Caveat: nudge "opened" stands in for "sent". Opening `/inbox?nudge=` with a fresh own nudge records an accepted outcome with `{ opened: true }` on the nudge's run, first write wins, in `after()` so refreshes and prefetches never write during render; a Gmail send is not tied back to the run, so the table cannot say whether the nudge was actually sent. Task suggestions are not counted, and a stale never-opened pre-draft reads as not used.


## D927. Background drafting pauses at 60 % of the monthly cap (#337 final review, 2026-10-13)

The draft queue checks this month's Assist spend (`monthSpend(monthKeyChicago(now))`, the same sum `runAssist` checks) against `BACKGROUND_CAP_SHARE` (0.6) × the pilot card's cap: read once per queue run, at the gate, where it returns `skipped: "background-cap"` before any other read. The figure is then cached: before every thread or quote that would make a call the queue checks the cached figure, re-reading the month's spend only after every 10 model calls (`BACKGROUND_SPEND_RECHECK_CALLS`), and stops with `stoppedBy: "background-cap"` once it is over. A run can therefore overshoot the 60 % line by at most about 10 calls. It applies to the queue only: interactive Draft reply, Suggest tasks, Inbox organization, the brief summary and Rebuild still run up to the full cap, so pre-drafting can never spend what a person needs by hand. A queue stopped by the guard still counts toward the 60 s per-owner gap, so Home loads don't re-read the month's runs on every view. The pilot card says "Background drafts pause at 60% of the cap." under the cap field. The share is a constant, not a setting.

## D928. A lazy brief never locks the slot to the counts (#337 final review, 2026-10-13)

A lazy build (20 s) that runs out of time before its Assist call used to store its counts-only fallback insert-if-absent, so the slot kept it all day. Now `loadBriefView` returns such a brief unstored and `transient` when its only failure is no time (`BRIEF_NO_TIME_ERROR`, `lazyBriefIsTransient`); the next view, or the cron, builds again (no model call is made when there is no time). As the one exception to "a stored brief is kept", `buildBriefsForAll` replaces a stored `builtBy: "lazy"` brief that has an `error` (`briefReplaceableByCron`) — but only with a cron build that has no error, and only after re-reading that the lazy brief is still the one stored (a Rebuild landing in between is kept; there is no blob compare-and-set, so the window is the re-read to the write). A Rebuild or cron brief is never replaced by the cron. The result counts it as `replaced`. A cron build that itself runs out of time before its Assist call is not stored either: the user is added to `skipped` and the first Home view builds the brief lazily.

## D929. Pre-drafts and nudges carry the owner they were made for (#337 final review, 2026-10-13)

`PreDraft.ownerId` and `AssistNudge.ownerId` record the user the queue drafted for. `preDraftFreshFor` / `nudgeFreshFor` (`src/lib/brief/fresh.ts`) require it on top of the basis check, and `readerPreDraft`, `nudgePrefill` (both now take `{ id, name }`) and the queue's `partDone` / `nudgeDone` use them, so a thread or quote reassigned since shows its new owner nothing of the old draft and the queue redrafts it for them. A stored draft without an owner (none were made outside this branch) reads as stale. The Home card's Draft ready / Send nudge chips follow the same functions.

## D930. A suggestion lives in blobs, not on a record (Estimate suggestion, #338, 2026-10-13)

An `EstimateSuggestion` (`src/lib/assist/features/suggestion.ts`, ids `ES-<base36>`) is stored as three kinds of blob (generic `blobs` rows) through `src/lib/stores/estimate-suggestions.ts`: `estsugg:<id>` holds the suggestion (every key written, absent values as `null`), `estsugg-src:<kind>:<sourceId>` names the source's latest suggestion (a re-run replaces it; the older suggestion stays readable), and `estsugg-quote:<quoteId>` names the suggestion a quote was saved from. No migration and no new field on comms, leads, surveys, meetings or quotes: a suggestion is a side record that nothing else needs to query, and a record field would put model output on a document that whole-doc writers (the Gmail import, `patchDoc`) rewrite. Ids are format-checked before every read or write, and a read whose blob doesn't match its id returns null. The cost is no listing or search across suggestions; the report reaches them only through the run detail's `suggestionId` (D939).

## D931. A POST route, not a Server Action (#338, 2026-10-13)

`/api/assist/suggest-estimate` (POST only, `maxDuration = 300`, `force-dynamic`) runs the extract + Opus draft, which can take a minute or two. A Server Action would take the `maxDuration` of whatever page calls it, and the entry points live on five pages (Inbox, Leads, venue assessment, meeting reader via the Inbox, Home's brief card), so one route with its own budget replaces raising each page's. `requireUser()` stays outside the try (a signed-out request redirects; the middleware does not exempt `api/assist`); a non-JSON body gets 415 before any work; settings, key and the `estimate` gate run inside the try, and every other answer is HTTP 200 JSON `{ok, suggestionId, href}` or `{ok:false, error}` with `cache-control: private, no-store`. The time-budget logic (`estimateBudgetFits`, `OUT_OF_TIME`) moved over unchanged.

## D932. Who can suggest from what: each source keeps its own screen's rule (#338, 2026-10-13)

Access is checked per kind before any model call, and every refusal costs no call and no run. **Thread:** `loadThreadFor`, a live email thread in the caller's own mailbox. **Lead** and **site visit:** any signed-in user, as on the leads page and the venue-assessments page. **Meeting:** `canSeeMeeting` (the reader's rule) **and** a customer link or a work link; an unlinked meeting is refused (`MEETING_UNLINKED_ERROR`) **even for its owner**, because a suggestion is visible to all staff and a private or internal meeting's notes must never land in one. The meeting reader shows the button only on linked meetings. A **lead's** prompt adds up to 3 threads linked to the lead (6 messages each), drawn **only from the caller's own mailbox** (`mailboxUser`, `visibleTo`, email only): another rep's linked mail is never read, though the suggestion built from the caller's own mail is visible to staff like any suggestion. All source text is wrapped as untrusted data (`<email_thread>`, `<lead_record>`, `<site_visit>`, `<meeting_notes>`; `SOURCE_UNTRUSTED_NOTE`), with the closing tags defanged inside.

## D933. Suggestions carry the lead, and the Estimator stamps `leadId` on create only; supersedes D877's "no leadId" (#338, 2026-10-13)

A lead-linked email, a lead, a site visit with a lead, or a meeting whose work link is a lead puts the lead id in the suggestion and in the Estimator link (`?lead=`). D877 kept `leadId` off the old throw-away draft quote; that reason is gone, since nothing is created until the rep saves, and a saved estimate rightly carries the lead's estimate number (migration 0030). The save action stamps it only in the **create** branch (`leadIdForCreate`: well-formed and the lead still exists, else nothing); the shared patch, and so every update, never carries `leadId`, and the client sends it only while the estimate has no id. A quote's lead is never changed by a later save.

## D934. The header is prefilled only when the customers match (#338, 2026-10-13)

A new estimate opened from a suggestion fills only what the URL left blank, and fills no lines. The customer is the URL's, else the suggestion's. Venue, contact and lead come from the suggestion only when the suggestion is about that same customer (`suggSameCustomer`), so an Estimator opened for one customer can never pick up another customer's venue or lead; venue and contact still go through `pickVenueId` / `pickContactName`, which drop a venue or contact not on the customer (a meeting's `siteId` that isn't one of the customer's locations is dropped). The suggestion's `quoteName` becomes the estimate's name when the URL has none (the spec's header list didn't name it; it is one line in `estimator/page.tsx`).

## D935. The first save links the suggestion; the first quote is kept; a missed link retries only through a save (#338, 2026-10-13)

A save that carries `suggestionId` calls `linkSavedQuoteToSuggestion` after the quote is written: the quote index `estsugg-quote:<quoteId>` is always written, but the suggestion's own `quoteId` keeps the **first** quote, which is the one the report scores. Unknown or malformed ids are ignored with no write. The client sends the id only until the link lands (`sendSuggestionId`: the view isn't `linked` and no save this session returned `suggestionLinked`). If the first link didn't land, the saved quote's page (URL still `?id=…&suggestion=…`) shows the suggestion unlinked so the next save retries, but only when `unlinkedRetryAllowed` holds: the suggestion is unclaimed or already this quote's, the quote was created no earlier than the suggestion, and when the suggestion names a customer the quote is that customer's. Nothing is written on a page load, so a crafted URL can't attach a suggestion to an older or another customer's quote just by being opened. The save action enforces the same guard server-side: on an update, `linkSavedQuoteToSuggestion` loads the suggestion and links only when `unlinkedRetryAllowed` holds for the quote being saved (its stored `createdAt` and customer), so a crafted save can't do what a crafted URL can't; a new quote may link any suggestion, and `linkSuggestionToQuote` never repoints a quote index that already names a different suggestion. A refused link just returns `suggestionLinked` false and never fails the save.

## D936. The panel's open state: per suggestion, remembered only when toggled, hidden by default on a saved quote (#338, 2026-10-13)

The Suggested BOM panel starts open on a new estimate and hidden behind its "Suggested BOM" tab on a saved quote. The open state is kept in `localStorage` under one key per suggestion (`suggestPanelKey`), read once per suggestion id after mount and wrapped in try/catch; it is **written only** when the user presses Hide or Show. Whether the estimate was saved is judged once at mount, so the save that gives a new estimate its id doesn't collapse the panel mid-session; the creator reopening the quote later, with nothing stored, gets it hidden. Nothing about the panel is stored on the server.

## D937. Unknown parts become unpriced custom lines marked "Suggested: needs a part and price" (#338, 2026-10-13)

`sanitizeSuggestion` keeps a SKU only if it is in the candidate set (catalog lines use the catalog's own description); any other SKU becomes a custom line from the model's description (else the stray SKU text), and a line with neither is dropped. Quantities are whole numbers 1–9999; the caps are 12 systems and **60 lines in total** (the old draft capped 60 per system), with `truncated` counting what the caps dropped. No price is ever stored in a suggestion. When the rep adds one, a live part is priced like a manual add (`addPart` / `catalogAddPrice` at the tier margin, system rounding as in `systemFromCategory`); a custom line, or a part that has left the catalog since, is added as an unpriced `custom` line with `internalNote: "Suggested: needs a part and price"`, so it shows as work to do and never as a $0 price the customer could see by accident. ✓ added is derived from the current sections (SKU, custom lines by description), never stored.

## D938. One busy-state helper for every entry point; any unreadable reply is one generic error (#338, 2026-10-13)

Every entry point is `<SuggestEstimate>` over `useSuggestEstimate` and `startSuggestion` (`src/lib/assist/suggest-client.ts`, which imports types only). A ref guard stops double clicks; the label is "Suggesting… (can take a minute or two)", or "Suggesting…" with the full text as its title where the header is crowded (`compact`, the venue assessment header). On success the button **stays busy** while `router.push` opens the Estimator, and recovers after 15 s (`SUGGEST_NAV_RECOVER_MS`) if the navigation never lands; the timer is cleared on unmount. `readSuggestResponse` accepts only an HTTP-ok `application/json` reply with `{ok:true, suggestionId, href}` whose `href` starts with `/estimator?`, or `{ok:false, error}` (capped at 300 characters, shown as is). A redirect to sign-in, a 5xx, a timeout page, a bad body or a network failure all read "Couldn't start the suggestion — try again." inline (`role="alert"`); the helper never throws. When the source already has a suggestion the control shows "Suggestion ready → Open" beside "Suggest again". The venue assessment's button is disabled while saving ("Saving…") or with unsaved edits ("Save your changes first"), because the route reads the saved record.

## D939. Report buckets: pending, no suggestion (including superseded), and discarded only for a deleted quote (#338, 2026-10-13)

A suggestion run (its draft run's detail has a `suggestionId` key) is scored off the suggestion's **first** quote with `estimateKeep` over the suggestion's catalog lines (custom lines aren't scored): accepted ≥ 90 % kept, edited, or discarded. No quote yet is **pending**. A quote that has since been deleted is **discarded**. A run that saved nothing (`suggestionId: null`: no systems, or the save failed) goes in its own **No suggestion** column, never discarded; so does a **superseded** suggestion: one with no quote whose source index now names a newer suggestion (Suggest again replaced it), which would otherwise sit in pending forever (`suggestionSuperseded`). A failed read of the source index leaves the run pending rather than guessing, and each read in `loadAssistVM` fails soft (`.catch(() => null)`), so one bad record can't blank the month. Legacy #334 runs keep `estimateOutcomeFor`. The feature row is now labelled "Suggest estimate (draft|extract)", which also relabels past months' Draft estimate runs, since they share the feature key.

## D940. Old #334 drafts keep their banner (#338, 2026-10-13)

`draftEstimateFromThread`, `draftEstimateAction` and the reader's Draft estimate button are gone, and nothing creates a quote from a model any more. `Quote.assistDraft`, `AssistDraftBanner`, `assistDraftViewOf` and `dismissAssistDraft` stay, so a draft quote made before this change still shows its notes, per-line reasons and Dismiss (which doesn't bump `updatedAt`). The `assist.estimate` feature flag, the `estimate` feature key, `ASSIST_MODEL_ESTIMATE` and the Opus draft step carry over unchanged; only the pilot card's label changes, to "Suggest estimate".

## D941. The brief's lead cue becomes Suggest estimate (#338, 2026-10-13)

On the AI daily brief card (#337), a Do-these-first row that is a lead shows "Ready to quote?" with the Suggest estimate control (and "Suggestion ready → Open" when the lead has one) when the viewer has the `estimate` feature; otherwise it keeps D923's "Ready to quote? → Open lead". `card-vm` sets `leadSuggest` only for a lead row that is in the triage snapshot, and the card looks up ready links only when the feature is on, bounded by the Do-these-first list (at most `SUGGEST_LOOKUP_MAX` = 20).

## D942. Converted leads keep Suggest estimate (#338 review, 2026-10-13)

The lead drawer shows Suggest estimate on a converted lead too, on its own line above the Convert / Lost / Delete row (or Open quote). A converted lead's suggestion uses `convertedCustomerId` when the lead has no `customerId`, so it lands on the customer the lead became, and the quote it seeds is stamped with the lead id like any create (D933): a second estimate for the same job is common, and it should carry the lead's number. The drawer reuses the page's loaded settings for the gate, skips both reads for anyone outside the pilot, and otherwise runs the gate and the ready lookup side by side.

## D943. Ask AI brings back an assistant, deliberately: reverses D89's removal and the #334 brief's non-goal (Ask AI, #339, 2026-10-13)

D89 (2026-07-19) deleted the "ask your business data" assistant along with the rest of the old AI layer, and the #334 Assist brief listed a chat assistant as a non-goal. Jeff asked for one on 2026-10-13 as roadmap piece 4 (the "AI sidebar"), so Ask AI reverses both on purpose. It is a fresh build on the Assist layer (`runAssist`'s gate, cap, rate limits and `assist_runs` log): nothing from the old `src/lib/ai/` comes back, D89's other deletions stay deleted, and D40's rule still holds — the model only looks things up and proposes; a person confirms every write. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-ask-ai-design.md`. Jeff asked to skip the per-section reviews, so the defaults below were taken without asking.

## D944. Ask lives in ⌘K search, and is unreachable at 860 px and below (#339, 2026-10-13)

The entry is a first row, **"✦ Ask AI: <query>"**, in the nav search dropdown (`Nav.tsx`), picked by click or ⌘↵ / Ctrl+↵; it opens a fixed Ask panel (`src/components/ask/AskPanel.tsx`, loaded with `next/dynamic`, ~520 px, full screen under 700 px). For Ask users the dropdown opens as soon as the query reaches 2 characters and shows "Searching…" until results arrive; everyone else's dropdown behaves as before, except that a reply for a query already typed past is now dropped (`latestQ`) for all users. The panel has no backdrop and an outside click doesn't close it; Esc (not one aimed at a select or date field, or mid-IME) or ✕ closes it and forgets the conversation, and a route change closes it too. Each opening starts a fresh conversation. **Open question for Jeff:** the nav search box is hidden at 860 px and below, so Ask has no entry on narrow windows, tablets in portrait or phones, and the native shell's tab bar has none either (spec non-goal). Not in pop-out windows (they have no nav).

## D945. Haiku answers; Try harder re-asks on Sonnet and replaces the answer only when it succeeds (#339, 2026-10-13)

Model slots `ask` (`claude-haiku-5-5`, effort low, `ASSIST_MODEL_ASK`) and `askHard` (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, effort medium, server-side fallbacks on, `ASSIST_MODEL_ASK_HARD`); both 4,000 max tokens, `maxRetries` 0, streamed. **Try harder** shows under the latest finished answer only — not mid-stream, not after Stop or a refusal, not on an answer already from Sonnet — and resends the conversation up to that question with `hard: true` and `retryOf: <runId>`. It counts as a question for the rate limit. The earlier run is marked `discarded` (owner- and feature-checked, first decision wins, `{retriedBy}` merged into its detail) **only when the retry was logged and ok**; an aborted, failed, refused or timed-out retry leaves the earlier run undecided. A run whose log failed (`runId` null) retries with `retryOf: null`. The pilot card's hint prints the effective model ids (env overrides applied). **Final review (2026-10-14):** Try harder also has its own limit, `ASK_HARD_PER_HOUR` = **15 per user per hour** (key `assist:ask-hard:<userId>`), checked before and on top of the shared 60/h, refused with "Too many Try harder requests — try again in a bit."; and it re-asks with the **original question's web setting** (kept on each answer), not whatever the toggle shows now.

## D946. Ask needs a Claude key and is Claude-only (#339, 2026-10-13)

`askGateFor(userId)` (`src/lib/assist/gate-server.ts`) passes only when the ordinary `ask` gate passes (`ASSIST_DISABLED` off, the user on the pilot list, the **Ask AI** switch on — it starts off, in `OPT_IN_FEATURES`) **and** the effective env has a non-blank `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (a key saved in Settings wins, D881). With `ASSIST_PROVIDER=local` and no key it refuses with "Ask AI needs the Claude API key." — the runner uses the beta Messages stream with server tools, thinking replay and `tool_choice`, which the local provider doesn't speak, so there is no local fallback. The same check decides the ⌘K row (the layout computes `askGateFor(...) === null` from its already-loaded settings; a failed check hides the row), the context chip and the runner. The runner then checks the monthly cap and `RATE_LIMITS.ask` = 60 questions per hour. A gate, cap or rate refusal is one `error` line with no `done` and no run. **Final review (2026-10-14):** between the monthly cap and the rate limits it also checks a **daily per-user budget**, `ASK_DAILY_USD_PER_USER` = $5: one SQL `SUM` of today's (Chicago midnight to midnight, by `createdAt`) logged `costUsd` for this user's `ask` runs (`userFeatureSpend`, next to `monthSpend`); at or over $5 it refuses "Ask AI daily limit reached — try again tomorrow.", same shape as the other refusals. Try harder adds its own 15/h limit (D945).

## D947. Conversation packing with no replay; refs are a server-side whitelist (#339, 2026-10-13)

Each question is a new series of model calls. Earlier turns are **not** replayed as assistant messages (thinking blocks are model- and conversation-bound, and Try harder switches model); the client sends the visible conversation (≤ 12 turns, ≤ 8,000 characters each, ≤ 40,000 total, last turn a non-blank user question, zod `strictObject`), and `packFirstUserMessage` builds one first user message: prior turns as untrusted `<turn>` blocks inside `<conversation>` (oldest dropped past 40,000), the page context as `<current_screen>` wrapping a `<record>`, "Today is …" (Chicago), then `Question:` and the new question. Within one question the loop replays the model's own assistant content unmodified. The client never sends refs. The link whitelist is built server-side per question from the page context's refs, every record a read tool returned, and the `[[kind:id]]` tokens in the conversation — the **newest 20** distinct tokens (newest turn first, latest token first within a turn, `priorRefTokens`), each re-checked with `resolveAskRef` under the asker's own access — and each is sent once as a `ref` event. A user-typed token counts only if the user can open it.

## D948. Loop limits; the final round keeps its tools with `tool_choice: none` (#339, 2026-10-13)

At most 6 model rounds and 12 tool calls per question (`nextRoundPolicy`): round 6, or the 12th call, makes the next round final; no round starts with ≤ 5 s left. Each tool result is capped at 6,000 characters (a 5,600 body before wrapping). Wall clock 60 s on Haiku, 90 s on Sonnet; each round's SDK timeout is the time left plus an abort timer; on timeout the answer keeps what it has and adds "Stopped — took too long." Calls beyond the limit get `is_error`; once the question is aborted or nearly out of time the remaining calls in that round get `is_error` "Not run — stopped." and aren't counted. Tools run one at a time (the dev DB is single-process). The **final round keeps every tool defined** (custom and web) and sends `tool_choice: {type: "none"}` plus an answer-now note after the tool results, because a request whose history holds `tool_use` / `tool_result` blocks must define tools, and an unchanged tool list keeps the cache prefix; a tool_use that still comes back is ignored. **This has not been verified against the live API** (no key on the build machine) — checked against the docs only. `refusal` → "I can't help with that one."; `max_tokens` → "…(cut off)"; `pause_turn` resumes once, only when the next round would be a tools round; an empty answer with no cards → "I couldn't find that." Unreadable streamed tool JSON (eager input streaming) re-issues the round once if no text went out, and is a cut-off (`max_tokens`, ok) once text has. **Final review (2026-10-14):** the re-issued attempt is still logged (and billed) as a round but **doesn't count toward the 6**, so a re-issued final round still gets its answer. **Caching:** each request carries two of the four allowed `cache_control` breakpoints — the system prompt (tools render before it, so they're cached with it) and, new, the **last block of the newest user message** (the first question or the latest tool results), so the growing conversation is read from cache by the next round. The breakpoint is added to a copy per request (`withConversationBreakpoint`), so earlier rounds' marks never pile up past the limit, and assistant content (thinking, tool_use) is never marked. The tool-input-JSON and web-400 checks match message text because SDK 0.128 has no typed error for either (the JSON one is a bare `AnthropicError`, the web one an ordinary `BadRequestError`); commented in `ask-runner.ts`.

## D949. Web search: off by default, `max_uses` 3 per round, version by model, carry on without it on a 400 (#339, 2026-10-13)

The web search server tool is sent only when the user turns on **Search the web** for that question. `max_uses: 3` applies per request — per model round — not per question, so with 6 rounds the worst case is **18 searches** (about $0.18 in search fees plus tokens); the tool-call cap doesn't bound server-side searches. Accepted for the pilot; if the report shows heavy use, drop the web tool after N searches. **Final review (2026-10-14):** the spend is now also bounded per person by the **$5 daily per-user Ask budget** (D946), which counts search fees with tokens in each run's `costUsd`, alongside the monthly cap and the 60/h and Try harder 15/h limits. Tool version by model: `web_search_20260209` for Sonnet 5.5 (Opus/Sonnet 4.6 and later), `web_search_20250305` for Haiku 5.5 and any unknown model from an env override (`web_search_20260318` exists in SDK 0.128 but isn't used). If Anthropic rejects the tool with a 400 that names `web_search`, the question is retried once without web and the answer says "(Web search wasn't available, so this answer uses Peak's records only.)"; any other 400 fails the question. Sources are text citations first, then raw results, http(s) only, ≤ 12 per question, titles ≤ 200 characters, opened in a new tab. Web search on Haiku has not been tried live.

## D950. Read tools see only what the asker can open; Ask's search is scoped to the asker's own mailbox (#339, 2026-10-13)

Eleven read tools (`src/lib/assist/ask-tools-server.ts`): `search`, `get_company`, `get_venue`, `get_quote`, `list_quotes`, `get_lead`, `get_project`, `get_thread`, `get_meeting`, `search_catalog`, `my_tasks`. Company, venue, quote, lead, project and catalog records follow their pages' rule (any signed-in staff). `get_thread` reads only through `loadThreadFor(id, me.name)` — a live email thread in the asker's own mailbox; `get_meeting` needs `canSeeMeeting` and never includes the transcript; `my_tasks` is the asker's own open tasks (not waiting on the customer) and assignments. A record the asker can't open reads exactly like a missing one ("Not found: …"), and that is a normal result, not `is_error`. `search` is the ⌘K core, extracted unchanged into `src/lib/search/global-search.ts` (the route's output is byte-identical), called with the new optional `{threadsOf: me.name}`, which limits the email-thread candidates in SQL (`searchDocs`' new `fieldEquals`) to the asker's own personal mailbox before the cut to 5, and each row is still re-checked with `loadThreadFor`. A lead's linked threads are listed from the asker's own mailbox only. Linked records get a ref only after a load confirms they exist; service records, meeting work links and task links print as text.

## D951. Lookup sizes: catalog pre-filter, newest-first threads, capped lists (#339, 2026-10-13)

`search_catalog` pre-filters in SQL (`listDocsFiltered`, a 10-field projection): live parts holding **every** query word (≤ 8 words) in any of SKU, description, manufacturer, MFR P/N, Model #, former SKUs or category, **≤ 400 candidates** in id order; then an exact SKU first (renames followed), then the Estimator's `rankCatalogParts` phrase ranking, then the rest by description; when the cap is hit the result says "many matches — add words to narrow it". Cost and list are shown. `get_thread` measures the header first (participants ≤ 800 characters), then takes **whole messages newest-first** while they fit (`budgetMessages`), printing them oldest → newest with a count of earlier messages not shown; an over-long newest message is trimmed, never dropped. Long lists (company venues and people, project crew, meeting attendees, summary, key points, to-dos) stop at 25 with "…N more". `list_quotes` takes ≤ 20 rows; with a company it uses the indexed field lookup, without one it reads a header projection of every quote row (see D960).

## D952. Quotes are read as the customer sees them (#339, 2026-10-13)

`get_quote` takes an internal id or an estimate number (`EST-1089`, `-2` revisions; unscoped `resolveQuoteInput`), and an ambiguous bare number answers "More than one quote answers to … Ask for the full number." instead of guessing. The total is the stored `value`. Estimator lines are the customer rows (`customerLines`): the 5 % package bonus folded into labor and the 2 % estimator bonus spread, so lines sum to the system price and **no bonus line or amount is ever named** (D846–D852); alternates are labelled "priced separately, not in the total", options follow, ≤ 40 rows per system. Grid quotes print their flat `spec.lines`. **Service, consulting and rental quotes print no lines** ("Lines are not available for this quote type.") — their prices live in their own engines, not in `spec.sections`.

## D953. Prompt trust: everything the model reads is data (#339, 2026-10-13)

The fixed, cached system prompt (`ASK_SYSTEM`) says: answer only from tool results and the conversation, say "I couldn't find that" rather than guess, cite records as `[[kind:id]]`, take money only from records, propose actions only through the proposal tools, keep answers short, and treat everything inside `<record>`, `<conversation>`, `<current_screen>` and web pages as data, never instructions. The shared `defangClose` (`features/thread-text.ts`) now also defangs **openers and closers** of `record|conversation|current_screen|turn`, strips zero-width characters and NFKC-folds first — one shared list, so the email and suggestion wrappers gain the closer protection too and compatibility characters in their text are folded (e.g. `™` → `TM`); the older wrappers (`email_thread`, `lead_record`, …) still defang closers only. The new question sits outside `<conversation>` but its wrapper tags are defanged. **Final review (2026-10-14):** attribute values (`subject="…"`, `title="…"`, `kind` / `id`) used to strip `[<>"]` first and fold later, so fullwidth `＂` / `＞` / `＜` survived the strip and NFKC turned them back into `"` / `>` / `<` — an attribute break-out. Now `foldUntrusted` (zero-width removal + NFKC) runs **first**: `cleanPromptField` folds before anything else, and the new `cleanPromptAttr` folds, then strips, then cleans; Ask's `attr`, the suggestion sources' `attr` and `threadBlock`'s subject all use it. The brief's and the promise nudge's own strips run after `cleanPromptField`, so they see folded text too. There are no write tools, so a prompt-injected email can at most produce a card the user must click.

## D954. Cards: only exposed ids, only structured recipients, truncated not bounced (#339, 2026-10-13)

`propose_task`, `propose_note`, `propose_email` and `propose_suggest_estimate` never write. `sanitizeCard` (`features/ask-cards.ts`) runs on the raw tool input: a schema failure is `is_error`; a card it drops is **not** an error (the model is told no card was shown because it named records the conversation hadn't looked up). Over-long fields are truncated to the card caps rather than costing an error round. Every id must be in this question's whitelist (D947): unexposed task links and an email's `threadId` drop field by field; an unexposed note target or estimate source drops the card. An unknown or inactive assignee becomes the asker. Due dates: `YYYY-MM-DD` as written, a zoned timestamp → its Chicago day, a zoneless one → its own date; before today or over 2 years out → none. **Email recipients** must have appeared in a structured field of a record this question exposed (contact and person emails, a thread's contact/cc and each message's From/To/Cc, meeting attendees) or have been typed by the user in a user turn — never from free text such as a message body. An email card whose recipients all drop survives with an empty To list, unless subject and body are both empty. Accepted risk: an inbound message's To/Cc are written by its sender, so a customer's email can put any address on the whitelist; the card only pre-fills a composer the user reviews and sends.

## D955. Each card confirms through the app's own write paths (#339, 2026-10-13)

Confirm buttons wait for the answer to finish (the run id arrives with `done`); after the card's own action returns a real ok, `recordAskCardAction(runId, kind)` (`src/lib/assist/ask-actions.ts`, `"use server"`) marks the run `accepted` (owner- and feature-checked, first decision wins) and appends the kind to `outcomeDetail.confirmed` (≤ 20; a run already discarded keeps counting confirms). **Task:** every task card goes through the new `createAskTaskAction` → `createAskTask` (`ask-task-write.ts`): title ≤ 200, notes ≤ 4,000, an active assignee (blank = me), the #327 +7 default due date, and exactly the card's links that still resolve under `resolveAskRef` (a thread through `loadThreadFor`, filed under section "Email" with `threadId` as the Inbox does; a venue kept only with its own company, or alone). Title, due, assignee and notes are editable inline. **Note:** company → `addCustomerNoteAction`; venue → the new `addVenueNoteAction` (the site `NoteRecord` the Krisp note decision writes, ≤ 4,000); lead → `logActivityAction({type: "note"})`, which now returns an error for a missing lead (**final review, 2026-10-14:** the lead card says so before you click — "Logs on the lead’s activity. If the lead hasn’t been contacted yet, this counts as its first contact for response time." — true to `logActivity`, which sets `firstContactAt` from a note only when it is still empty; the SLA rule is unchanged); project → the new `addProjectNoteAction` (never redirects). Company and venue notes post `customer` on the pop-out channel; lead and project notes post nothing (#336 has no such entity; other windows catch up on focus). **Email:** nothing sends — the card writes `{to, subject, body}` to this tab's sessionStorage (`peak-ask-compose`) and opens `/inbox?compose=ask&n=<nonce>`; the Inbox reads it once after mount, removes it, ignores it after 5 minutes, and opens a **new** message (not a reply) with the signature; the body never goes in the URL. **Suggest estimate:** `startSuggestion(source)` (#338); on success the panel navigates to the Estimator and closes — but if the panel was closed meanwhile it doesn't navigate, and the suggestion stays reachable from its source.

## D956. Page context: every quote builder, the meeting reader's `?m=`, and a chip that never carries record text (#339, 2026-10-13)

`parsePage` (`features/ask-page.ts`) maps `/companies/<id>`, `/venues/<id>`, `/estimator?id=` **and** every builder `quoteBuilderHref` hands out (`/flame-tests/quote`, `/repairs/quote`, `/inspections/quote`, `/design/engagements/quote`, `/rentals/quote`, all `?id=`), `/inbox?thread=`, `/inbox?view=meetings&m=` (the spec's `meeting=` was wrong; `thread=` is ignored in the meetings view), `/leads?lead=`, `/projects/<id>` and `/venue-assessments/<id>`. The runner loads the same summary as the matching `get_*` tool under the same rule (a survey uses #338's `surveyText` without its `<site_visit>` lines) into `<current_screen>`. `GET /api/assist/ask/context?page=` answers only `{ref, title}` or `null` (gate off, page over 500 characters, unknown or forbidden page, error — always 200, `private, no-store`) from `parsePage` + `resolveAskRef`, never the summary. The chip's ✕ drops the context for follow-ups; the first question's context is resolved even if ✕ is pressed before its answer arrives.

## D957. Answers render as text; a link needs a matching ref (#339, 2026-10-13)

`renderAnswerBlocks` (`features/ask-render.ts`) produces React text nodes only — paragraphs, bullets, `**bold**`, `#` headings shown bold; there is no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in `src/components/ask/` (pinned). A `[[kind:id]]` token links, titled by the record, only when a `ref` event for that exact kind:id arrived in this conversation **and** its href is site-relative (no `//`, `/\`, whitespace or control characters); otherwise its id prints as plain text. A plain click navigates the main window and closes the panel; Shift-click pops out a thread, quote or company (#336) and otherwise acts as a click. A part links to `/catalog?q=<sku>` (anyone can open it; a renamed SKU keeps the requested id), a task to `/queue`, a meeting to its reader. "Looked at N records" counts refs that arrived after the first lookup's status, so page-context and earlier-answer refs whitelist links but aren't counted (a record a tool returns that the page already exposed isn't listed).

## D958. One logged run per question, billed from the stream (#339, 2026-10-13)

`POST /api/assist/ask` (`maxDuration = 120`; 415 for a non-JSON content type before any work, then `requireUser` with `unstable_rethrow` so sign-in still redirects, 400 for a bad body, otherwise a `no-store` NDJSON stream) runs `runAsk`, which never throws. Every question that passes the gate logs one `assist_runs` row: `feature "ask"`, `step null`, the last round's answering model, `fellBack`, usage summed over rounds, `costUsd` = per-round Claude cost + web searches × $0.01, `output` ≤ 20,000 characters, `error` (null / declined / timed out / aborted / the message), `contextRef "ask:<kind:id|none>"`, `outcomeDetail {rounds, toolCalls, refs ≤ 50, cards, cardKinds ≤ 20, web, hard, retryOf}`. Usage is tracked **as stream events arrive** (`message_start`, `message_delta`), so a round that aborts, times out, errors or is re-issued is still billed for what streamed; only usage after the last delta seen can be under-counted. A client disconnect aborts the stream and the run is still logged. Runtime failures send `error` then `done`; an abort sends no error. **Final review (2026-10-14):** "never throws" now holds for the pre-run checks too — a failure loading the settings or the key, in the gate, or in the monthly / daily spend sums is one `error` ("Ask AI couldn't answer — please try again.") with no run, like a gate refusal. A **401 or 403 from Anthropic** (`AuthenticationError` / `PermissionDeniedError`, or that status) shows "The Claude API key was rejected — check Settings → Beta → Assist pilot." instead of the generic failure; the run is still logged with the SDK's message as its `error`.

## D959. The Assist report gains an Ask AI table (#339, 2026-10-13)

`askReport(runs)` (`src/lib/assist/report.ts`, pure), shown on the Assist pilot card after the Daily brief table: one row per person plus All — questions, answered on Haiku / Sonnet (substring match on the answering model; anything else is counted but not shown), Try harder count and rate (runs with `outcomeDetail.hard === true` — **final review, 2026-10-14:** was `retryOf`, which is null when the earlier answer's log failed), cards proposed by kind (`cardKinds`; older runs that logged only a count show under cards shown), cards confirmed by kind, web searches and cost. The feature row is labelled "Ask AI".

## D960. Known gaps left as follow-ups (#339, 2026-10-13)

(1) **⌘K itself still lists other mailboxes' email-thread subjects** — a pre-existing behaviour of the global search, unchanged here because `globalSearch` without options must stay byte-identical for ⌘K; Ask's own search is scoped (D950). (2) `list_quotes` with no company reads a header projection of every quote row and filters in JS; revisit past ~10k quotes. (3) Lead and project notes from a card post nothing on the pop-out channel, because #336's `ChangedEntity` has no lead or project kind. (4) If the Inbox composer is already open when an email card is confirmed in that tab, the open composer keeps its own state.

## D961. One engine absorbs Venue Assessments and the rigging-inspection capture (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's brainstorm decision 1. Venue Assessments (`FS-####`, `surveys`) becomes the Quote and Conditions tiers on the new engine in slice 2; the rigging inspection's capture moves onto it in slice 3, while `RI-####` keeps its job / quote / renewal / report shell. There is one findings register everywhere. Slice 1 touches neither: Venue Assessments stays where it is in the nav and no `FS` or `RI` record is migrated. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-13-assessments-engine-design.md`.

## D962. Definitions are code-first, with stable keys and admin-addable pick lists (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 2. Scopes, modules, questions and the R/F/G/L/A/H/X gate rules are versioned TypeScript data in `src/lib/assessments/defs/` (`types.ts`, `scopes/*.ts`, `rules.ts`, `picklists.ts`, `index.ts` with `ASSESSMENT_DEF` version 1). Keys are stable and dotted (`rigging.overhead`). An in-app form builder comes later, built on the same definitions. Admins can add pick-list values from day one (Assessments → Pick lists, settings blob `assessment_picklists`, `src/lib/stores/assessment-picklists.ts`); code values can't be removed or renamed, and an added value can be retired but not deleted while a stored answer uses it. Each assessment is stamped with `defVersion`; a meaning-changing edit needs a new version. Unknown keys from a newer client are stored and ignored.

## D963. One rating scale on every finding, with a legacy map for later slices (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 3. Every finding is rated Immediate attention / Needs attention / Good; answers add N/A and Unable to inspect. Priority (H/M/L) and budget tier are separate columns. The legacy map in `src/lib/assessments/findings-model.ts` applies when slices 2 and 3 land: RI Poor/urgent → Immediate; RI Fair/necessary and FS Replace → Needs attention; RI Good/basic → Good; FS Monitor → Good plus the Monitor action tag. Nothing reads it in slice 1.

## D964. Finding ID is `CUSTOMER-VENUE-CAT-###`, from short codes (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 4, with his venue-code rule. Companies and sites get a short code (`companies.short_code`, `sites.short_code`, migration 0040). The company code is the initials of the name, 2–6 characters (Manitowoc Public School District → `MPSD`). The venue code is the first three letters of the first meaningful word of the venue's location name; the, of, st, st. and saint are skipped (Lincoln High School → `LIN`, Wilson Middle School → `WIL`, Washington Middle School → `WAS`, St. Norbert College → `NOR`). Initials are not used because school names would collapse into `?MS` / `?HS`. A collision within the same scope gets a digit suffix (`LIN2`). Suggestion rules live in `src/lib/assessments/codes.ts`. The printed form is `MPSD-LIN-RIG-003`; every finding also keeps a stable internal key `fd_…` that all links use.

## D965. The fourth tier is a per-curtain flame test plus service checks (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 5, for slice 4: per-curtain pass / fail / retreated with NFPA 701 tag and photo, rolling up into the flame-test job's existing tallies; fire-curtain drop test, emergency lighting and re-inspection as short single-scope visits. Nothing is built in slice 1 beyond the gate rules (F1–F5) the condition visit already carries.

## D966. Customer output is a report now and the portal later (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 6. Slice 1 delivers a printed/PDF report and the register. The portal register, acknowledgment, immediate-hazard alerts and due-date reminders are slice 5. Assessments and findings are not in the portal.

## D967. The first slice is the Condition assessment (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 7, driven by the Manitowoc (MPSD) case. The `condition` visit type turns on S0–S7 (S2 at screen depth); S8 can be switched on. Every checklist line in the Manitowoc "Every venue", "Rigging triage" and "Power and control" sections maps to a question key, and `scripts/test-assessments.ts` asserts it against `docs/assessments/manitowoc-coverage.json`. The brief's R7 (full rigging intake) is defined but unreachable until slice 3. Peak does rigging inspections, so RIG findings route to a Peak rigging inspection; electrical, structural and hazardous-materials findings route to outside specialists and are flagged, never rated.

## D968. Data shape: three collections, `assessments`, `findings`, `venue_profiles` (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 8, migration `drizzle/0040_assessments.sql`. `assessments` is per visit (`AS-####` from 1001); `findings` is the register across visits (doc id = the `fd_` key); `venue_profiles` holds carry-forward facts (doc id = the site id). Each is a doc table with its `seq_bump` trigger, registered in `src/db/doc-tables.ts` and `src/db/seed-data.ts`; stores are `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`, `findings.ts` and `venue-profiles.ts`. The migration is idempotent (D141). Its header and some code comments carry the number #337, which was the pre-merge guess for this item; the real number is #340.

## D969. No bulk import of the CESA 10 audit items in slice 1 (#340, 2026-10-14)

Jeff's decision 9. The audit reference and estimate are typed per finding (`Finding.auditRef`). A bulk import is not planned for any slice yet.

## D970. R1 "no overhead rigging" still shows the pit lift and the access/fall module (#340, 2026-10-14)

The brief says to skip every other rigging question when overhead rigging is none. A pit lift isn't overhead rigging, and a catwalk is a fall hazard regardless, so the pit lift and the grid / bridge / catwalk access + fall module stay visible. This deviates from the brief's literal wording. `src/lib/assessments/defs/rules.ts`, `defs/scopes/rigging.ts`; found in review.

## D971. Conditionally worded required photos are optional (#340, 2026-10-14)

Required photos worded "every gap", "any…", "if posted/visible", and the named photo set, are marked `optional` on their `PhotoReq`: the editor offers them as slots, but they never count as Mark-complete gaps, because the evaluator can't know whether the condition applied. `missingPhotos` in `src/lib/assessments/evaluate.ts` skips optional requirements; types in `defs/types.ts`.

## D972. Five flagged-answer prompts were added beyond the brief — assumed default, ask Jeff (#340, 2026-10-14)

Taken from the Manitowoc checklist and added to the rule set in `src/lib/assessments/defs/rules.ts`: exits blocked → GEN / Immediate; trap door or pit unguarded → GEN / Immediate; no e-stop → RIG / Needs attention; no hold-to-run → RIG / Needs attention; panel clearance under 36" → ELC / Needs attention. They are not in the brief's X5 table. **Assumed default — ask Jeff** to confirm the five prompts, their categories and their ratings (PUNCHLIST #340, Remaining).

## D973. An empty answer counts as unanswered; Clear sends a marker (#340, 2026-10-14)

An answered value of `""`, `[]` or null counts as unanswered in `evaluate()` and in the progress rings. The editor's Clear sends `{ state: "answered", v: null }` (the clear marker), because the per-key merge never drops a key: an explicit, newer answer with no value is how a field gets emptied. `src/lib/assessments/answers.ts`, `evaluate.ts`, `[id]/question.tsx`.

## D974. Answers merge per key, newest `at` wins; the server stamps `by` and clamps `at` (#340, 2026-10-14)

Two people walking different scopes of one visit don't overwrite each other. `mergeAnswers` (`src/lib/assessments/answers.ts`) never drops a server key. On every save and push the server overwrites `answer.by` with the session user and clamps `answer.at` to now + 5 minutes, so a client clock can't win every merge. Other fields use the store's `rev` check. `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`.

## D975. Assessments can only be started online (#340, 2026-10-14)

Client-minted `AS-` ids are unsafe under max+1 numbering, so `/api/sync/push` never creates an assessment (`pushAssessment` in `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`, called from `src/app/api/sync/push/route.ts`); the id comes from `/assessments/new` (`new/actions.ts`). Answers, photos and findings all work offline once an assessment exists. A finding created offline doesn't have this problem: its key is a random `fd_` id and its printed ID is allocated on sync (D980).

## D976. An offline push never loses capture: rejects go into `syncRejects` (#340, 2026-10-14)

Invalid items, late pushes to a completed assessment, and scalars dropped as stale are written by the server to the record's `syncRejects` list instead of being thrown away. The editor shows them in a banner with Re-enter / Use mine (`[id]/sync-banners.tsx`, `src/lib/assessments/editor-model.ts`). The online save path (`[id]/actions.ts`) refuses loudly instead, since the user is looking at the screen. `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`, `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`.

## D977. Rev contract: adopt the returned `rev`; the push base is `sent − 1` (#340, 2026-10-14)

Callers adopt the `rev` the store returns. The push base rev is `sent − 1`, the outbox convention, and only dirty scalar fields are sent. `photoSetOffered` is sent only when dirty. `src/lib/assessments/editor-model.ts`, `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`. Found in the Task 5 review.

## D978. Findings created offline are accepted after the assessment is completed (#340, 2026-10-14)

The register must never lose capture, so `pushFinding` accepts a finding for a completed assessment (the online save refuses it). The report tolerates a late finding that resolves an overridden gap. `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`, `src/lib/assessments/report-model.ts`.

## D979. A finding's category is frozen once it has a printed number (#340, 2026-10-14)

The printed ID embeds the category and its per-category sequence, so changing the category would change the printed text. To change it, void the finding and create a new one. `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`, `src/lib/assessments/findings-model.ts`.

## D980. Printed IDs are allocated under an advisory lock; voided numbers are never reused (#340, 2026-10-14)

The server allocates `NNN` as max+1 per (company code, venue code, category) under a Postgres advisory lock (namespace 337, key `customer:site:category`; the lock helper is in `src/db/index.ts`). Voided findings keep their number and it is never reused. Codes are resolved first, outside the transaction. The exclusion across connections is proven only on PGlite; it is checked in production after the merge deploy applies migration 0040, with a throwaway customer — not on a preview, because previews skip migrations (`scripts/migrate.mjs`) and their company and venue reads would fail without `short_code` (PUNCHLIST #340, Remaining 4). **Final review:** the number is also unique per printed prefix across code changes (D997). `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`, `src/lib/stores/assessment-rows.ts`. The namespace number 337 is the pre-merge item number and is kept so the lock key doesn't change.

## D981. Inline (base64) photos are dev-only (#340, 2026-10-14)

When Vercel Blob is off, the shrunken photo is stored inline on the assessment so the editor works in local dev without touching the production Blob store. Production refuses or strips inline photos; real photos live in private Blob under `assessments/<AS-id>/<photoId>.jpg`. `src/lib/assessments/photos.ts`, `photo-bytes.ts`, `photo-queue.ts`, `src/app/api/assessments/[id]/photos/upload/route.ts`. The dev inline cap allows about one photo.

## D982. Photo ids are `p_` + hex with no hyphens (#340, 2026-10-14)

One photo's id can't alias another's blob path. The upload broker also re-checks that every path is under the assessment's prefix and never trusts a client path. `src/lib/assessments/photos.ts`, the broker `src/app/api/assessments/[id]/photos/upload/route.ts`.

## D983. Photo uploads that can't succeed become terminal (#340, 2026-10-14)

When the server says no retry can succeed (or a photo is over 7 days old) the photo is marked `failed`: the drain skips it, the bytes stay on the device, and the editor lists it with Retry / Discard. A stuck pending photo can be removed from the Mark-complete dialog. Photos still waiting or failed hard-block Mark complete. `src/lib/assessments/photo-queue.ts` (IndexedDB), `[id]/photo-button.tsx`, `[id]/complete-dialog.tsx`.

## D984. The print route inlines photos as data URIs (#340, 2026-10-14)

No photo-route token and no middleware change: `/print/assessment/[id]` reads each photo through `photoBytes` (`src/lib/assessments/photo-bytes.ts`) and embeds it, so the headless Chrome render needs no extra authenticated fetch. The inline budget is 20 MB; past it a photo prints a placeholder. `src/app/print/assessment/[id]/page.tsx`, `src/lib/assessments/report-data.ts`.

## D985. Merging a finding voids it with a structural `mergedInto` (#340, 2026-10-14)

A merged finding is voided with `mergedInto` pointing at the survivor. It resolves its prompt only while the chain of `mergedInto` links ends at a live finding. Merge and split each run in one transaction under a per-assessment advisory lock (`merge:<assessmentId>`), so a failure part-way rolls everything back. `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`.

## D986. Quote these findings opens the repair builder intake, not a code-created quote (#340, 2026-10-14)

Quote these findings → Repair quote opens the repair builder with `?findings=`, which shows a banner and prefilled scope lines (category, venue, printed ID in the text); the quote is linked on its first save, with venue-checked keys. It does not create a zero-priced quote in code, so the repair builder's own pricing stays in charge. The Estimator variant creates a draft and links it. `src/app/(app)/repairs/quote/page.tsx`, `controls.tsx`, `actions.ts`, `src/lib/assessments/quote-from-findings.ts`, `findings-quote.ts`.

## D987. Quote ↔ finding links are quote-level `findingKeys` plus the printed ID in the line text (#340, 2026-10-14)

Not a line-level `findingKey` as the spec said: the line sanitizers drop unknown keys. The quote carries `findingKeys`, and each line's text starts with the printed ID so customer documents show it. `src/lib/stores/quotes.ts`, `src/lib/assessments/findings-quote.ts`.

## D988. A link failure after the quote exists never reads as "not saved" (#340, 2026-10-14)

If linking findings fails after the quote was created, the quote is kept and a notice says the link failed, so the user doesn't save again and create a duplicate quote. `src/app/(app)/repairs/quote/actions.ts`.

## D989. Short-code setters normalise; a regular save never touches a code; a code locks once used (#340, 2026-10-14)

`setCompanyShortCode` / `setSiteShortCode` trim and uppercase. A regular company or site save never writes or clears a code. A code is editable until a non-voided finding uses it, then locked; changing it after that needs `approve`. Issued printed IDs keep their text, and new findings continue the sequence under the new code. If the company or venue has no code at the first finding, the server assigns the suggestion. `src/lib/identity/companies.ts`, `sites.ts`, `src/lib/assessments/codes.ts`, `src/components/assessments/short-code-edit.tsx`.

## D990. Assessments sits in the Customers nav group after Venue Assessments (#340, 2026-10-14)

The spec said a Field group; there is none. Every `/assessments/*` route lights the Assessments child. `src/components/nav/nav-data.ts`.

## D991. The report is emailed as an Inbox draft (#340, 2026-10-14)

The spec said to attach from the composer's existing document picker, but the composer has no picker. **Email report** on the report page renders the PDF and creates an Inbox draft with the PDF attached, tied to the customer. The draft has no link chip and nothing is sent. `src/app/(app)/assessments/[id]/report/actions.ts`, `report/toolbar.tsx`. **Final review:** the PDF is stored in Blob and attached by reference, not inline (D999).

## D992. The PDF render waits for the report-ready marker, and PDFs are streamed (#340, 2026-10-14)

`renderPrintRouteToPdf` waits for the `waitFor` selector to stop matching, so the report waits on `[data-assessment-report]:not([data-report-ready])` and the marker is set once photos decode (`src/components/assessments/report-ready.tsx`). The routes stream the PDF instead of buffering it, because a buffered response over about 4.5 MB fails on Vercel. Per-step render budgets sum to 105 s inside the routes' 120 s `maxDuration`. `src/lib/assessments/report-pdf-server.ts`, `src/app/api/assessments/[id]/report-pdf/route.ts`, `findings-pdf/route.ts`; print token kinds `assessment` and `assessment-findings` in `src/lib/quote-pdf/token.ts`.

## D993. There is no in-app findings-only report page (#340, 2026-10-14)

The register and the venue card link straight to the findings-only PDF (`/api/assessments/findings-pdf`, print route `/print/assessment-findings/[scope]`). The spec's `/assessments/findings/report` page was not built; the PDF is the deliverable. `src/components/assessments/findings-report.tsx`.

## D994. `venue_profiles` survive the go-live wipe; assessments and findings are demo data (#340, 2026-10-14)

Venue profiles are carried-forward facts about real venues, like venues themselves; assessments and findings made before go-live are test data. Short codes are kept. `venue_profiles` is listed in `CONFIG_COLLECTIONS` in `src/db/seed-data.ts`, which the wipe skips.

## D995. Save actions return `{ ok: false }` instead of redirecting (#340, 2026-10-14)

Assessment and finding save actions use `getOptionalUser` + `can("create")` and return `{ ok: false }` when the user is signed out or lacks the permission, so a background autosave never navigates away and drops on-screen answers. `src/app/(app)/assessments/[id]/actions.ts`, `findings/actions.ts`.

## D996. Merging findings needs only `create` (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

Merge (and split) stay on the `create` permission, not `approve`. Both are field operations inside one open assessment: every finding must belong to the same assessment, the assessment must not be completed, and the merged-away findings are voided with `mergedInto` (never deleted), so their numbers and history survive and the merge is auditable. Gating it on `approve` would stop the assessor tidying up duplicate findings on site. `src/app/(app)/assessments/[id]/actions.ts` (`mergeFindingsAction`, `splitFindingAction`), `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`.

## D997. Printed IDs are unique per printed prefix, across code changes (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

After an approved code change (venue LIN → LN2) another venue of the company can take LIN, and numbering per venue alone would issue `…-LIN-RIG-001` a second time. The next number is now 1 + the highest `seq` over both the findings of this venue + category and every finding whose printed ID starts with the same prefix (`${companyCode}-${siteCode}-${category}`), voided and deleted ones included. Allocation takes an advisory lock on `printed:<prefix>`, then the venue lock, then the finding's own lock — always in that order — so two venues sharing a prefix can't race. `printedPrefix` in `src/lib/assessments/findings-model.ts`; `maxSeq` / `allocatePrintedId` in `src/lib/stores/findings.ts`.

## D998. A push that throws is `retry`; the editor folds this device's outbox entry before it saves (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

`/api/sync/push` gains a per-record `retry` status. `pushAssessment` and `pushFinding` reply `retry` for anything thrown (a lock timeout, a database error) and keep `error` for permanent refusals (no permission, an unknown or malformed id, a different venue). The SyncEngine leaves a `retry` entry pending and flushes again after 30 s; an unknown status still parks as `error` (`pushOutcome` in `src/lib/sync/engine.ts`). On mount the editor reads this device's outbox entry for the assessment (`engine.outboxEntry`) and folds it in before any save (`foldOutboxEntry` in `src/lib/assessments/editor-model.ts`): answers merge per key keeping their original `at`, missing photo refs and dismissed prompts are added as dirty, and a queued scalar is taken only when the entry was built on the current rev — otherwise it is reported as dropped. An online save then clears the entry only when it covers it (`outboxEntryCovered`, passed to `recordSynced` through the new `keepOutbox` option of `saveThroughOutbox`). A completed assessment's entry is left to the push, which records it in `syncRejects`. An entry that takes 10 consecutive `retry` replies (counted on the entry as `retries`, reset on `ok` and on re-enqueue; `retryOutcome` in `src/lib/sync/engine.ts`) is parked as `error` with "The server kept failing to save this — it will retry when you edit again", so a deterministic server throw does not retry every 30 s forever.

## D999. Email report stores the PDF in Blob and attaches it by reference (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

`navData` reads every comms doc on every page, so a multi-MB base64 PDF must not sit in one. With Blob configured, Email report stores the render at `assessment-pdfs/<AS-id>/<ms>.pdf` (Blob adds a suffix) and the draft carries `pdfPath` + `href` (`/api/assessments/<id>/report-pdf?file=…`), the way Estimator Phase 3 attaches quote PDFs; it is still refused past 10 MB. The Gmail bridge reads it only when `assessmentPdfFitsThread` passes — an assessment PDF path, an existing assessment, and a thread for that assessment's customer or one with no customer and no link; never a quote-linked thread — and streams the bytes from Blob. Without Blob (local dev) the PDF rides inline up to 1.5 MB; above that Email report says "Report is too large to email from this computer — download it instead". Stored report PDFs are not removed by the go-live wipe. `src/lib/assessments/report-pdf-path.ts` (pure), `report-pdf-storage.ts`, `report-model.ts` (`emailAttachmentMode`), `src/lib/gmail/bridge.ts`, `src/app/api/assessments/[id]/report-pdf/route.ts`.

## D1000. The editor's save status follows the outbox (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

The header label is derived, not remembered: `saveStatusLabel` (`src/lib/assessments/editor-model.ts`) reads the editor's last save, the SyncEngine's connected state and this assessment's outbox entry, re-read on every SyncEngine change, so it changes when the outbox drains. Errored entry → "Couldn't sync — <reason>"; queued and offline → "Saved on this device — will sync when you're back online"; queued and online → "Syncing…"; nothing queued → "Saved".

## D1001. Unknown answer keys are capped per assessment (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

Answers to keys the definition doesn't know (a newer client's questions) are kept, but at most 100 such keys and 200 KB of them per assessment, counting what is already stored; a re-answered stored key replaces its old size. Over a cap the action refuses the save, naming the key; a push records the answer in `syncRejects` and keeps the rest. Known questions are never capped. `capUnknownAnswers` in `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`.

## D1002. New assessment checks its links (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

`createAssessmentAction` refuses, before anything is created, an assessor who isn't an active user and a lead, site visit or project that doesn't exist or belongs to another customer. A linked record that names no customer yet (a fresh lead) can't belong to another one, so it is accepted. `checkAssessmentLinks` in `src/lib/stores/assessments.ts`, `src/app/(app)/assessments/new/actions.ts`.

## D1003. Ask AI's search returns assessment and finding rows without links (#340 final review, 2026-10-14)

Ask AI's `search` tool is the ⌘K core (`globalSearch`), so since #340 it also returns **Assessments** (`AS-####`) and **Findings** (printed IDs) rows. They print under "(no link)" with their ids: there is no `assessment` or `finding` ref kind. Adding one means a new `RefKind`, an href, a loader and a `resolveAskRef` case in `src/lib/assist/ask-tools-server.ts` — more than the two-line change the final review allowed — so it is left for a later slice.

## D1004. An email thread is visible only when it is yours, assigned to you, or deliberately linked (#341, 2026-10-14)

Jeff, 2026-10-14: "you can only see information that was either linked to entities or your own information." One pure rule, `canSeeThread(t, me)` in `src/lib/stores/comms-visibility.ts` (re-exported from `comms.ts`; `me` is the user's name, the shape `mailboxUser` and `assignedTo` hold): the thread is not in Deleted **and** it is in my own mailbox (`visibleTo`, which now needs a non-blank name), **or** — not being another person's draft — it is assigned to me, **or** it is **deliberately** linked to an entity (D1005). Every surface that shows thread content to someone other than its owner reads through it: the Inbox reader (D1006), the company page and activity feed (D1009), ⌘K (D1010), Ask AI's read tools (D1011) and an admin's view of a teammate's Start here (D1015). Background code that never shows one person's mail to another (the Gmail bridge, the system backfill, quiet-quote checks, the brief's own-mailbox builds) is unchanged. Meetings keep their own rule (`canSeeMeeting`). Another person's draft is never visible even when linked: unsent mail is not yet a record. `isOwnThread` (own and not in Deleted), `isSharedThread` (deliberately linked, live, not a draft — the viewer-free rule) and `hasDeliberateLink` sit beside it.

## D1005. "Linked" means deliberately filed or linked; the automatic sender match stays private (#341 fix 1, 2026-10-14 — Jeff's ruling)

The review of the first cut found the import, `applyResolution` and `resweepThreads` stamping `customerId` whenever the sender is a known contact — so adding a contact could expose another person's mail. Jeff decided: a thread is shared only once its owner, or Inbox organization acting for them (#335 filing, including auto-filing on reply and sender rules), files or links it to a company, quote, lead, project or venue. **The flag:** `CommThread.linkedBy?: "user" | "filing"` (`src/lib/stores/comms.ts`). Set only on deliberate paths: `linkThread` (default `"user"` — the link sidebar / panel, quick-add customer / venue, the venue card, + New quote; `"filing"` from #335 `fileThread`), a thread created in the app with a picked customer or record (`create()` — Compose, Log call / meeting, renewal outreach, an estimate or report email), the record picker's customer adopt (`setLinkAction`) and Schedule site visit's adopt, and a Peak/Customers label a person adds in their own Gmail (a label that only echoes the customer the app already holds keeps the flag as it was). Never set by `applyResolution`, `stampResolutionOnCreate`, a resweep or `setIdentityMessage`; `applyResweepPatch` clears it when it changes the customer, and removing a Peak/Customers label clears it. Undo of a filing restores the flag it found (`FilingApplied.customer.linkedBy`, `restoreThreadIdentity`). Creating a task from an email does not link the thread (no thread field changes) and so does not share it; + New quote from an email does (it links the thread to the quote). **Linked fields** then count — `customerId`, `siteId`, a work `link` with both type and id, `linkedContactIds` — only when `hasDeliberateLink(t)` holds: `linkedBy` is set, or `filing.state === "filed"` (not noise), or one of the legacy proofs (D1012). `resolvedContactId` never counts. "Assigned to me" compares like `sameName` (trimmed, case-insensitive), the test Morning triage's email feed uses.

## D1006. Off-mailbox threads open read-only; every Inbox write stays with the owner (#341, 2026-10-14)

`?thread=` opens a thread only when `canOpenThread` passes (`canSeeThread`, plus the owner opening their own thread from Deleted); anything else reads as no thread selected. It never switches the box to another person's mailbox, and `?draft=` opens only my own draft. A thread outside my mailbox renders read-only: a banner ("In Jeff Chesebro's mailbox — read only", or "Shared mailbox — read only" for a legacy shared-box thread; "· linked to <company>" only from the thread's own deliberately linked `customerId`, never the automatic `resolveCustomerId`), the message history, and nothing that writes — no reply / forward / call log, Owner, Mark replied / Close / Reopen, Archive, Site visit, Suggest tasks, Draft reply, Suggest estimate, pre-made draft, link sidebar, per-message Link… / Task… / link picker, or court strip — and it is never marked read. **Fix 1:** the read-only payload carries no link, task or customer data either (`linkOptions`, `taskLinks`, `threadTasks`, `customerCard`, `suggested`, `candidates`, `linkedPeople`, `siteOptions`, `contactOptions`, `customerOptions` empty; `resolvedCustomerId` null; new `readOnlyLinkedTo`).

`src/lib/inbox-thread-guard.ts` (`ownThread`, `ownThreadIds`) is the one check: the thread must sit in the signed-in user's own mailbox (`visibleTo` — Deleted included, so restore and mark-read still work in the Deleted folder). Added to every action in `inbox/actions.ts` that takes a thread id (read / unread, archive / unarchive, flag, pin, category, delete / restore, the six bulk actions, status, reopen, assign, record link, message link, reply, call note, sending or saving an existing draft), to `linkThreadToCustomerAction`, `dismissSuggestionAction` and `quickAddCustomerAction`, and to `createSiteVisitAction`'s customer adopt. A refused id answers like a missing thread. **Fix 1:** the harness now generates the audit list from the source — every exported async function in the seven Inbox thread-action files whose parameter list carries a thread id — so a new unguarded action fails `test:thread-visibility`.

## D1008. Actions and drafting stay own-mailbox only (#341, 2026-10-14)

`loadThreadFor` (own, live, email) stays the rule for Draft reply, Suggest tasks, Suggest estimate and the brief's pre-made drafts — a reply goes out from that mailbox. A task's thread link also stays own-only, everywhere: the Inbox's Create task already required it, and Ask's task card now does too (`createAskTask` checks a thread with `loadThreadFor`; a thread read from another mailbox carries `readOnly` on its server-side ref and `sanitizeCard` never puts it on a card, so the card shows only what it will write). The exception is Morning triage's Done / Reassign for an assignee (D1014).

The company page's Communications list reads `visibleByCustomer(id, me)` (`byCustomer` filtered by `canSeeThread`) and its activity feed `loadCustomerFeed(cust, me.id, me.name)` (the same rule); the vendor page and the company summary, which have no viewer, keep `isSharedThread`. A teammate's thread that sits on the company only through the automatic sender match is not listed; Deleted threads and other people's drafts never are. The subject and last-message snippet stay for what is listed — a deliberately linked thread is a shared business record by Jeff's rule — and each row opens the Inbox reader, read-only for anyone but the owner.

## D1010. ⌘K cuts thread candidates to the viewer's rule in SQL, before the per-group limit (#341, 2026-10-14)

`searchDocs` gains one additive option, `where: DocCond` — a tiny predicate language (`all` / `any` / `is` / `isNot` / `isFolded` / `filled: "text" | "array"`) over the doc's JSON, every path segment and value a bound parameter (`docCondSql` in `src/db/doc-store.ts`). `canSeeThreadCond(me)` is `canSeeThread` written in it, branch for branch (the `linkedBy` flag, a filed filing and the legacy proofs included); `globalSearch` passes it for the comms candidates and re-checks each row with `canSeeThread`, so other people's private mail can't crowd the visible threads out of the 100 candidates or the 5 shown. A test asserts the SQL and the JS rule agree on every fixture for two viewers. The route still passes `session.user` (its name is now read); the output shape is unchanged; Deleted threads are gone from ⌘K, mine included. `GlobalSearchOpts.threadsOf` is replaced by `emailOnly` (Ask's search). This closes D960 (1) and #339's ⌘K follow-up.

## D1011. Ask AI reads follow the same rule (#341, 2026-10-14)

`loadThreadReadable(id, me)` (`src/lib/assist/thread-access.ts`): a live email thread that passes `canSeeThread`. `get_thread`, the `search` tool (through `globalSearch`'s rule, email threads only), `resolveAskRef`'s thread case (so page context and re-checked earlier tokens) and `get_lead`'s thread list (every live email thread linked to the lead, any mailbox — a work link is deliberate) read through it.
